body:
## Governing chain

Addendum to Priority 1, UMR-20260806-171945-5767 ("single deterministic
orchestrator: one entrance, one exit, boolean output contract").

Real Tier-1 independent audit posted to PR #249 at 2026-08-13T06:15:24Z
(head `ce649278`), verdict **AUDIT:FAIL**: `worker-exit-status-bridge.py`
in that PR is deliberately, permanently restricted to never write
`umr_tasks.status=completed` -- by design (see that file's own module
docstring, point 1: "a clean exit code is NOT evidence of substantive
completion"). PR #249 therefore only closes the failure/blocked half of
the write-back gap. **This PR closes the SUCCESS half**, without
re-opening or re-auditing PR #249 and without touching
`worker-exit-status-bridge.py` at all.

## Zero-duplication finding (HARD REQUIREMENT 4)

Ran `resource_governor.py --query-umr --search` and checked
`wiring_registry`/`capability_registry`/`MASTER_INDEX.yaml` before writing
anything, per the SPEC. Found a real, already-built, already-tested,
already-audited mechanism that does exactly this job and was simply never
wired to run periodically:

- **`reconcile_owner_dispatch_status.py`** (this repo, added under
  UMR-20260806-075726-babc, hardened against a real AUDIT:FAIL on its own
  PR #147) -- scoped precisely to `umr_tasks` rows with
  `source_trigger='owner_dispatch_gateway'` and `status='running'`
  (exactly the shape of all six SPEC-named rows). Cross-references three
  independent real signals: `systemctl --user is-active`, real
  `task.yaml`, and real `gh pr list`/`gh pr view` state (PR matched by
  branch name, plus AUDIT:PASS/FAIL freshness vs the PR's current head
  SHA). Deterministic bucketing, never AI narration:
  - real PR **MERGED** -> `completed`
  - real PR **CLOSED** (not merged) -> `failed`
  - no PR ever opened, unit dead -> `killed`
  - real PR still **OPEN** (even with a fresh AUDIT:PASS) -> always
    `NEEDS_AI_JUDGMENT`, **never** auto-terminalized
  - unit genuinely active -> left alone

Its own `wiring_registry` row records `cron_scheduled: false` -- it
existed on disk with a real test suite (`tests/test_reconcile_owner_dispatch_status.py`)
but **zero periodic caller**. That is the actual root cause of the
"success half" gap: not a missing mechanism, a missing wire.

I did **not** write a new reconciler. I wired the existing one in, and
fixed one real, live-confirmed data-quality bug in it (below).

## What guards the success write (HARD REQUIREMENT 2)

`worker-exit-status-bridge.py` is untouched -- still never writes
`status=completed`, still fails closed on any ambiguous exit. The success
write in this PR goes through a **completely separate, already-audited**
evidence path:

1. `systemctl --user is-active <unit>` confirms the unit is genuinely not
   running (never touches a live unit).
2. The row's own real `task.yaml` (`repo`/`branch`) is read to find a
   real PR via `gh pr list --repo <repo> --state all` (branch-name match,
   not a task.yaml self-report).
3. Only a real `gh pr view` state of **MERGED** ever produces
   `new_status="completed"`. An OPEN PR -- even one already carrying a
   fresh `AUDIT: PASS` comment -- is **never** auto-terminalized
   (`classify_row()`'s own long-standing rule, unchanged by this PR): see
   `tests/test_reconcile_owner_dispatch_status.py::test_open_pr_never_auto_terminalized_even_with_fresh_audit_pass`.
4. The only DB write path is `apply_correction()` -> `update_umr_task()`
   (enforced by `test_apply_correction_writes_only_via_update_umr_task`,
   which stubs the connection to raise on any raw `conn.execute()` write).

No AI self-report anywhere in this decision. Every completion is a
computed boolean from real, independently-verified GitHub/systemd state.

## Changes in this PR

1. **`reconcile_owner_dispatch_status.py`** -- `apply_correction()` now
   also passes `ts_completed` and a real evidence-carrying `reason` to
   `update_umr_task()`. Live-confirmed bug: `update_umr_task()` only ever
   writes the columns it's explicitly given, and the pre-existing code
   never passed either -- so every row this script ever corrected,
   *including genuine completions backed by a real MERGED PR*, kept
   `ts_completed=NULL` and `reason='queued'` forever. Both new values are
   derived from the exact same evidence dict already computed by
   `classify_row()` -- no new guess, no second evidence source.
2. **`status-remediation-tick.py`** -- new `run_owner_dispatch_reconciliation()`,
   called from `main()` on every real ~10-minute tick
   (`veridian-cron-status-remediation-tick`), gated by the same `--apply`
   flag this script's own remediation already uses (dry-run by default;
   the live unit already passes `--apply`). Loaded in-process via the
   same `importlib` pattern this file already uses for
   `generate_wiring_registry.py` -- no new subprocess, no new systemd
   unit. Per the `~/.config/systemd/user/README.md` **STANDING RULE**
   ("closed set of 18/19 periodic jobs... a new periodic need that fits
   one of these goes in as a new step inside the matching existing
   unit/script, not a 20th unit"), this is wired as a new step inside the
   existing `status-remediation-tick` unit/script -- **no new `.service`/`.timer`
   was created.**
3. **Tests**: `test_apply_correction_sets_ts_completed_and_reason` (new,
   in the existing suite) + a new file,

Real bug (UMR-20260813-042207, addendum to P1 UMR-20260806-171945-5767, finding 1 of 3): `resource_governor.py --query-umr --umr-id X` returned the WRONG (most recent) row regardless of X.

**Root cause:** the CLI parsed `--umr-id` into `args.umr_id` but never threaded it into `query_umr_tasks()`, which had no `umr_id` parameter at all. Any `--umr-id` call silently fell through to the plain-listing branch (status/tier filters only, `ORDER BY ts_submitted DESC`) and returned the newest row in `umr_tasks`, ignoring X. `--search` (FTS5) was unaffected, which is why it worked as a documented workaround.

**Fix:**
- `query_umr_tasks()` gains a real `umr_id` kwarg: exact match on `umr_tasks.umr_id` (the real PRIMARY KEY), as its own first-priority branch ahead of `task_identity`/`query_text`/plain-listing.
- `resource_governor.py`'s `--query-umr` handler now passes `umr_id=args.umr_id` through.
- `tests/test_query_umr_by_id.py`: real regression test against a scratch DB (3 rows, oldest/target/newest all sharing status+tier) proving `--umr-id X` returns exactly the row where `umr_id=X`, both at the function level and through the real CLI subprocess. Verified this test fails (count=3, returns newest) against pre-fix code and passes against the fix.

Three real, previously-uncommitted-or-vulnerable pieces of work, landed together per Owner direction — this hardens the stop-work-order gate before it ships further, rather than as a follow-up patch.

## 1. Stop-work-order gate hardening (`resource_governor.py`)

Following a real, independent tier1 review of the first version (merged via PR #272) that found two genuine security gaps:

- `_git_committed_file_text()` read raw local HEAD in whatever branch happened to be checked out in the shared AI_OS directory — never verified it was on trunk or pushed anywhere. A purely local, unpushed git commit satisfied the gate with zero GitHub review. Confirmed live: the shared directory was found checked out on an unrelated branch whose HEAD was exactly such a commit. Now pinned to a real, bounded-timeout fetch of `origin/main` (configurable via `VERIDIAN_GOVERNOR_STOP_WORK_TRUNK_REF`), failing closed on any fetch failure rather than falling back to a stale cached ref.
- `stop-work-order-lifted` entries lifted EVERY order in `STOP_WORK_ORDER_TASK_IDS` unconditionally, with no check on which specific order the entry actually named. Now scoped per-order (`_stop_work_order_lifted_for()`), matching only on the real order_id string in the entry's own scope text — same convention as the existing exemption-scope matcher.
- Bonus fix found while reading this code closely: the entries loader as merged was missing the dict-unwrapping for the real YAML file's actual top-level shape (a dict with a `decisions` key, not a bare list) — meaning the shipped gate could never find any real entry at all. Restored.

11/11 real tests pass (9 original + 2 new regression tests for the two hardening fixes), including a real two-repo (work + bare `origin`) fetch fixture proving an unpushed local-branch commit does NOT satisfy the gate when a real trunk ref is configured.

## 2. master_issue_tracker CRUD (`superboss-register.py`)

`add-issue`/`close-issue`/`update-issue`/`list-issues` — the one real, permanent, callable write path into the already-live, already-986-row `master_issue_tracker` table (previously only writable via a one-off `/tmp` script). The real PreToolUse hook that blocks unbounded root-filesystem walks (UMR-20260806-121825-8ece, real incidents that drove load average to 28.86). Was already live and in active use this entire session but never committed. 19/19 real tests pass.

Full suite: 420/421 pass. The one failure (`test_timer_is_really_enabled_and_active`) is a live systemd-state check for an unrelated subsystem (`veridian-build-lock-liveness-guard.timer`), not touched by anything in this PR.

## Governing chain
UMR-20260807-112306-4e60, citing UMR-20260807-061238-ae93, UMR-20260807-070110-5ea7, UMR-20260807-070904-736a, UMR-20260807-035145-aa45, UMR-20260807-040704-992a.

## Real problem (found live, this session)

All 5 governing-chain UMR rows showed `status='running'` in `umr_tasks` with `last_heartbeat=NULL`, while `systemctl --user is-active` for every one of their real units returned `inactive`. `journalctl --user -u <unit>` for each confirmed the real worker **and** its supervisor review both exited `status=0/SUCCESS` cleanly (not a stall/crash) — real timestamps and PIDs in the task notes below. This matches the already-known "worker exits cleanly but umr_tasks status never reconciles" class of bug (separately being closed for the write side by PR #249 / task-20260807-052027).

`resource_governor.py`'s own sanctioned, evidence-based reconciliation tool for exactly this shape is `--backfill-null-heartbeats` (`backfill_null_heartbeats()` → `_task_yaml_for_umr_row()` → `_forward_progress_decision()`, cross-checking real `gh pr view` state before ever writing `failed`). Trying to reuse it (scoped to just these 5 rows, to respect a hard "do not blanket-sweep other running tasks" limit) surfaced a **real bug in `_task_yaml_for_umr_row()` itself**: it only tries (1) `task_docs.get(row['task_identity'])` and (2) a `reconcile-umr-<id>` directory-name fallback. For an `owner_dispatch_gateway`-dispatched row, `task_identity` is a synthetic `owner-task-<ts>-<pid>` string that is never a real `TASKS_DIR` directory name, and none of these 5 real child task directories contain `reconcile-umr-` either — so **both existing paths miss all 5**, and the function would have silently returned `None`, causing `backfill_null_heartbeats()` to default all 5 to `'failed'`.

That would have been wrong per real evidence:
| UMR | real child task | task.yaml status | real PR | real PR state |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| UMR-20260807-061238-ae93 | task-...-081903-mandatory-execute-the-rebuild | blocked | #254 | OPEN |
| UMR-20260807-070110-5ea7 | task-...-081909-confirmed-with-fresh-evidence | completed | #253 | **MERGED** |
| UMR-20260807-070904-736a | task-...-081913-amendment-to-umr-...-5ea7 | blocked | #256 | OPEN |
| UMR-20260807-035145-aa45 | task-...-053227-amendment-to-umr-...-171945 | blocked | #251 | OPEN |
| UMR-20260807-040704-992a | task-...-053232-second-amendment-to-...-171945 | blocked | #250 | OPEN |

4 of 5 have real, live, open forward progress; 1 is genuinely merged. None are genuinely dead/failed.

## Fix

Add a third lookup path to `_task_yaml_for_umr_row()`: derive the real child `task_identity` from the row's own `unit_name` column (`veridian-worker@<child_task_id>.service` → `<child_task_id>`) before falling back to the `reconcile-umr-` scan. Confirmed live that `task_status_sync()` already has a correctly-keyed entry for all 5 real rows under exactly this derived id — the data already exists, the lookup just never tried it.

No behavior change for rows that already resolve via path 1 or (now) path 3 — verified by the full existing test suite still passing unmodified.

`python3 -c "import py_compile; py_compile.compile('resource_governor.py', doraise=True)"` — OK.

## Scope note

The 5 target `umr_tasks` rows themselves were already reconciled directly (not via this PR/merge) using a small scoped script that imports `resource_governor.py` and reuses `_task_yaml_for_umr_row`/`_forward_progress_decision`/`sbr.update_umr_task` exactly as `--backfill-null-heartbeats` would, filtered to only these 5 `umr_id`s — never a raw SQL write, never touching the other ~43 unrelated `running`/`NULL`-heartbeat rows live on the DB right now (hard scope limit for this task). ## Summary
Owner directive 2026-08-07: **one input gate, one output gate** for `superboss-register.sqlite`. Real problem confirmed via grep: 46 separate scripts each open their own raw `sqlite3.connect()` to the live DB.

Lands the already-drafted, already end-to-end-tested single-writer HTTP gateway (`/opt/veridian/ai-os/superboss_gateway_DRAFT_2026-08-07.py`) into this repo, reviewed (not rewritten), plus its persistent systemd unit.

## What's included
- `scripts/superboss_gateway.py` — stdlib-only local HTTP JSON gateway on `127.0.0.1:8790`:
  - `GET /health`
  - `POST /read {"table", "where", "limit"}`
  - `POST /write {"op": "insert"|"update", "table", "values", "where"}`
  - Table allowlist (`umr_tasks`, `wiring_registry`, `capability_registry`, `ai_agent_registry`, `knowledge_engine`, `owner_priority_sequence`, `owner_priority_override`) + `PRAGMA table_info()` column validation, never raw caller SQL.
  - Single in-process write lock serializes writes; reads use a separate `mode=ro` connection and run concurrently (matches the DB's existing WAL-mode concurrency, already live: `journal_mode=wal`, `busy_timeout=5000`).
- `systemd/veridian-superboss-gateway.service` — persistent singleton daemon (`Type=simple`, `Restart=on-failure`, `WantedBy=default.target`). Not a periodic/cron unit, so it's not subject to the `~/.config/systemd/user/README.md` closed-set-of-19 STANDING RULE (explicitly scoped to periodic jobs). Same category as the already-live `veridian-glm-proxy.service` / `veridian-governor-tick.service`.

## Independent verification performed before landing
- `py_compile` clean.
- Re-ran the draft live myself (not just trusting the SPEC's claim): `GET /health` → `{"ok": true, "journal_mode": "wal"}`; `POST /read` on `umr_tasks` returned a row that matches a direct `sqlite3` `SELECT` on the real DB exactly; `POST /read` on `sqlite_master` correctly rejected (`"table not allowlisted"`).
- Confirmed live DB path `/opt/veridian/ai-os/memory/superboss-register.sqlite` is real (8023 rows in `umr_tasks`, `journal_mode=wal`).
- Checked the deterministic briefing's 2 pointers, both non-blocking: `wiring_registry` match is this task's own self-referential dispatch_event row; `capability_registry` "task_oa" is an unrelated Next.js AI-orchestration API route, not a DB gateway — no real duplicate exists.

## Explicitly out of scope (per SPEC)
None of the 46 existing scripts are migrated to use this gateway. That is separate, larger follow-up work, tracked as its own future task.

## Post-merge steps (tracked in PROGRESS.md)
- Sync `/opt/veridian/scripts`, install + `daemon-reload` + `enable --now` the unit, confirm `systemctl --user status` active and real `curl 127.0.0.1:8790/health` → `ok:true`.
- Register `capability_registry` row `superboss_gateway`.

body:
## Root cause
`worker-entrypoint.sh`'s every exit path calls `veridian-task.py checkpoint`, which
writes task.yaml/CONTROLLER.yaml plus an audit-log row via
`superboss-register.py log-action` -- but never touches `umr_tasks.status`.
`umr_tasks.status` is set to `'running'` once, at dispatch time, and nothing in the
worker's own lifecycle ever writes it again. Every self-disabling "give up, no more
retries" path (budget cap, preflight hard stop, quality-gate exhausted) exits 0
(`ExecMainStatus=0`, `Result=success`) with no automatic path back to a terminal
`umr_tasks` status. Confirmed live: 24 real rows in this exact shape during this fix's
own verification run (ages 0.9h-5.3h).

## Fix
- `systemd/veridian-worker@.service`: add `ExecStopPost=`, which systemd guarantees runs
  on every stop (clean exit, non-zero exit, `TimeoutStopSec`, `SIGKILL`, OOM-kill) --
  unlike the entrypoint's own `trap ... EXIT`, which cannot fire once the shell itself is
  SIGKILLed.
- `worker-exit-status-bridge.py`: the ExecStopPost hook. Only ever writes
  `umr_tasks.status=failed`, and only for a definitive, already-self-reported negative
  outcome (task.yaml's own last checkpoint status in
  failed/blocked/cancelled/rejected_duplicate/superseded/not_needed). Never writes
  completed/completed_unmerged from a process exit code. Never touches a `pending_review`
  (supervisor handoff) or `in_progress`/`pending` (possible pending systemd retry) row.
- `reconcile_stale_running_workers.py`: one-time (safely re-runnable) sweep over the
  existing backlog. Scoped to `status=running` rows bound to a `veridian-worker@` unit
  whose `ActiveState` is not active. Resolves the real task dir from
  `outputs_json.new_task_id`, decides from real artifacts only via the existing
  `mark-umr-terminal`/`reset-umr-to-queued` CLI (never raw SQL, never exit-code-based
  completion).

## Real one-time run (already applied against the live DB)
24 examined: **3 completed, 17 completed_unmerged, 1 requeued, 3 skipped** (genuinely
still active). Full per-row JSON report in this task's own PROGRESS.md
(`veridian-ai-os` repo, `task-20260807-052027-platform-integrity--worker-units-exit-0`).

body:
PM override dispatch: task-20260807-002908-pm-overrides-a-false-positive-credit-acc, reuses child UMR-20260806-182453-702a from blocked task-20260806-205209.

## Why this is a fix, not a new tool
The credit-accountant's zero-duplication rejection was overridden as a false positive: the artifact it matched (`generate_platform_completion_checklist.py`) is itself the defective thing, producing 5 non-reproducible Scripts-section readings (47/148 -> 45/150 -> 47/152 -> 0/154 -> ...) with no real platform change between them. This PR fixes that exact script **in place** — no replacement, no parallel script.

## Root causes (both reproduced, not theorized)

**Denominator drift**: `_list_scripts()`/`_list_test_files()` glob()'d the live, shared `/opt/veridian/scripts` checkout directly. Confirmed live: multiple concurrent sessions' uncommitted/in-flight `.py` files sitting in the scanned dirs at investigation time, each traced to a real in-flight PR against this repo.

**Numerator collapse to zero**: reproduced directly with a 2-file local repro (one valid test, one with a real `SyntaxError`) — pytest aborts the **entire** run with `returncode=2` ("Interrupted: N errors during collection") the instant even one requested file fails to collect, and the old classification logic then marked every *other*, fully-passing file as "error" too (since it only special-cased explicit `FAILED`/`ERROR ...` lines for the specific failing file, then fell back to "error" for everyone else whenever `returncode not in (0, 1)`). One transient/incomplete concurrently-written file was enough to zero the whole Scripts numerator.

**Fix**: every script/test discovery, content read, and pytest run now goes through a `git archive HEAD` snapshot extracted into an isolated temp dir — never the live working tree. `git archive` only ever extracts fully-committed, atomic blobs, so a concurrent session's mid-write file structurally cannot appear in the snapshot. `git_head` is recorded in the JSON/MD output for verifiability.

## Incidental finding (documented, NOT fixed here — separate scope)
While proving the fix, found `superboss-register.sqlite` has real, live corruption (`PRAGMA integrity_check`: out-of-order rowids, wrong index entry counts on 2 b-trees), which raises plain `sqlite3.DatabaseError` — not the narrower `OperationalError` this file already caught — crashing the whole script on any read of the affected tables. Broadened the existing per-table/per-query `except` clauses from `OperationalError` to `DatabaseError` (its own real parent class) so one corrupted table degrades to `complete_and_tested=False` instead of taking the entire run down. This does **not** repair the corruption itself — that needs its own separate decision/escalation.

## Proof (Step 4 requirement)
3 consecutive real (non-`--skip-tests`) runs at the same `git_head`:
- Scripts section: **byte-identical** across all 3 (md5 match on the isolated `scripts` JSON payload; 150 scripts; real pytest "2 failed, 543 passed" every run)
- Tables/Search totals stable (36/46, 10/11) across all 3; only the live `actions` table's own `row_count` (and its FTS shadow's hit count) drifted between runs — expected, real concurrent DB writes, exactly as the module docstring already documents as correct variance, not instability

## Real current numbers (post-fix)
Scripts 42/150, Tables 36/46, Search 10/11.

Does not touch OCID-020, the Z.AI track, or the Owner absolute stop-work order (task-20260806-165921, already completed) — out of scope per the override's own explicit boundary.

Real dispatch: UMR-20260806-161614-5850 (parent UMR-20260802-165606-4413, OCID-020).

## What this fixes

`gtm_check_deployment_testing.py` (GTM certification category_index=21,
"deployment testing") had two real bugs found this session:

1. **Missing credential injection.** The script correctly *detected* a real,
   working Vercel token (`VERCEL_ACCESS_TOKEN` in `/opt/veridian/shared/.env`,
   loaded via systemd `EnvironmentFile=` for worker units — confirmed this
   run: `vercel whoami` with that token → exit 0, real account `fchecklist`)
   but never actually passed it into the `vercel ls` subprocess call, so it
   hit vercel's interactive auth path and timed out at 60s every time despite
   a working credential being available.

   Fixed by injecting the real token into the subprocess's own env as
   `VERCEL_TOKEN` (the vercel CLI's own standard env var — confirmed to work
   with no `--token` flag needed). Deliberately **not** a `--token` CLI arg:
   a real manual test this run showed that leaks the token into both `ps`
   and vercel's own echoed pagination-hint output. Evidence output is also
   defensively redacted for the real token value before being written to
   `evidence_json`.

2. **stdout/stderr bug**, found via the first fix's re-run. Under a captured
   (non-TTY) subprocess, the real vercel CLI writes its deployment status
   table (the only place `Ready`/`Canceled` text appears) to **stderr**, not
   stdout — confirmed directly this run (`'Ready' in stdout` → False,
   `'Ready' in stderr` → True, same real invocation). The original status
   check only inspected stdout, so it would **always** report "no Ready
   deployment found" (a false fail) regardless of real deployment state.
   Fixed by checking both streams combined.

With both fixes, a real re-run against compliance-tracker's real linked
Vercel project produced a real, honest `pass` verdict — real Ready
deployments confirmed in real `vercel ls` output — recorded via the
canonical `gtm_write_category_result.py` writer, never raw SQL.

body:
Implements approved proposal 86 (`pm_decisions_pending` id=86, status=approved), child UMR of `UMR-20260806-135902-cf13`, governed by `UMR-20260806-071025-1d28`.

## Real confirmed incident
Live DB grew 2034MB->4067MB in ~11 min (13:44-13:55Z, 2026-08-06). `umr_tasks` alone was 1855.7MB. Every `owner_dispatch_gateway`-sourced row carried a `metadata_json.reuse_check_result` averaging 6.7-7.1MB, dominated by `reuse_check_result.wiring.matches` (one sampled row: 8441 items, 5.97MB) and `.knowledge.matches` (379 items, 841KB).

## Root cause
`superboss-register.py`'s `lookup_entity()` FTS query against `wiring_registry_fts` (and `query_knowledge()`'s analogous query against `knowledge_engine_fts`) had no `LIMIT` clause, returning every matching row. `plan_generator.py`'s `check_reuse_before_dispatch()` (called by `resource_governor.py`'s `submit()` on every dispatch) then embedded that full unbounded result verbatim into `metadata_json.reuse_check_result`.

## Fix (both halves of the approved scope)

**Step 1 (superboss-register.py)**: added `WIRING_LOOKUP_MATCH_LIMIT` / `KNOWLEDGE_QUERY_MATCH_LIMIT = 50` to the two named FTS queries. FTS5's own `ORDER BY rank` already sorts most-relevant-first, so 50 keeps far more candidates than a human/agent reviewer could usefully scan (~5-10) while leaving real headroom against rank noise. No existing internal LIMIT precedent to match — `lookup_capability()`'s own analogous query was checked and found equally unbounded (left alone, out of approved scope for this UMR).

**Step 2 (plan_generator.py, defense-in-depth)**: `check_reuse_before_dispatch()` now independently truncates every match list it returns to `EMBEDDED_MATCH_SUMMARY_LIMIT = 10`, adding a real `total_matches` count so "how many exist" is preserved even though the full dump is not. Holds even if a future caller reaches `lookup_entity`/`_query_knowledge` some other way, or Step 1's LIMIT is later reverted/bypassed.

**Step 3**: `tests/test_reuse_check_unbounded_metadata_fix.py` — real scratch-DB tests (3000 synthetic `wiring_registry` rows + 200 `knowledge_engine` rows, all matching one query) proving both bounds hold end-to-end via the real reuse-check path. Real measured result: **14155 bytes** for the full `metadata_json`, vs **7128106 bytes** observed for ONE real row pre-fix (**503.6x smaller**).

## Verification
- 320/320 existing repo tests pass (`python3 -m pytest tests/`), no regressions.
- New test file: 4/4 pass standalone and under pytest.

## Mandatory condition honored
No existing row's `metadata_json` was deleted, rewritten, compacted, vacuumed, or truncated — this only bounds *future* writes. The reuse-check itself (zero-duplication enforcement) is not disabled, only bounded.

Real problem: veridian-cron-prune-memory-backups.timer's original once/day (04:47 UTC) OnCalendar could not keep up with the real observed same-day backup creation rate. Real evidence measured 2026-08-06: two ~2.1GB superboss-register.sqlite copies (pre-wiring-backup, pre-systemd-backup) were created 7 minutes apart (13:30Z, 13:37Z) -- a real observed rate that can exceed 4GB/10min -- while the timer's next fire was still ~14 hours away.

Fix (two parts):
1. New `veridian-cron-prune-memory-backups.path`: event-based primary trigger, fires the existing prune service immediately when a new file appears under ai-os/memory or ai-os/memory/backups, so it cannot be outrun by creation rate.
2. `veridian-cron-prune-memory-backups.timer`: OnCalendar raised from once/day to every 5 minutes as a clock-based backstop. Justification: bounds worst-case missed-event exposure to about one real backup (~2.1GB observed) against ~33-35GB real free space at time of fix, comfortably below the observed >4GB/10min peak rate.

Also tracks `veridian-cron-prune-memory-backups.service` in this directory for the first time (was live since PR #151 but never version-controlled).

This is a trigger-mechanism change to the already Owner-authorized unit #19 (UMR-20260806-084306-f599 Step 6), not a new unit-#20 under the closed-set STANDING RULE -- documented as such in systemd/README.md and each unit file's header.

Governing: UMR-20260806-071025-1d28. Task: UMR-20260806-134738-eec3.

## UMR-20260806-130914-e7f1 (governed by UMR-20260806-071025-1d28)

Real dispatch alleging a "false completion" for `UMR-20260806-122546-78d6`. Independent verification (governing session) found the PM's underlying concern partly right and partly mis-framed:

- **Confirmed accurate**: the row's `outputs_json` is genuinely `{}`, `logs_ref` is genuinely `None`.
- **Correction to the PM's framing**: `gh pr view 171` shows a real, genuine, committed PR (commit `2290b1b`, authored 2026-08-06T12:54:50Z) matching the row's own `--reason` text exactly. This is **real work**, just sitting on an unmerged, open PR (#171) -- not a fabrication. Root cause: `mark-umr-terminal` (added by PR #164) never had an `--outputs-json`/`--commit-sha`/`--file-path` parameter at all -- a real **mechanism gap**, not caller discipline. `update_umr_task()` already supported an `outputs` kwarg; the CLI simply never exposed it.

## Fix

1. **`mark-umr-terminal --status completed`/`completed_unmerged` now structurally require real, independently-verified evidence** before the row is ever written:
   - a real `--commit-sha` that IS a real ancestor of `origin/main` (checked live via `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, mirroring `triage_owner_umr_24h.py`'s own `is_commit_on_main()`), **or**
   - a real `--file-path` that genuinely exists on disk.

   A real commit that exists but is **not yet** an ancestor of main (the real "PR open, unmerged" case) is refused for `--status completed`, with a message pointing at the new `completed_unmerged` status instead. Refusal = non-zero exit, `refused: true` JSON, row left completely untouched.

2. **New `completed_unmerged` status** (added to `UMR_STATUSES`) -- the honest, distinct state for "real work done, real commit exists, not yet merged." Follows this repo's own existing `<state>_unmerged` naming precedent (`closed_unmerged` in `backfill_ocid_registry_phase2_columns.py`). Deliberately *not* folded into `UMR_ACTIVE_STATUSES` or reused as `dispatched` -- the AI-side work is genuinely done, so it must not be treated as still-in-flight by existing stale-row sweeps. Live `CHECK` constraint widened via a real, `_write_lock()`-protected DROP+rebuild+RENAME migration, verified safe under 8-way concurrent `init` invocations against a real pre-existing-schema fixture (no deadlock, no corruption, clean `PRAGMA integrity_check`, zero data loss).

3. **`_write_lock()` made safely re-entrant** within one process (plain depth counter) -- required because `_ensure_umr_table()` now reaches the new migration and is already called from inside an existing `_write_lock()` via the `init` CLI command; a naive nested acquisition would self-deadlock. Cross-process mutual exclusion is completely unaffected.

4. `dispatch-owner-task.sh`'s mandatory completion instruction extended to name the new requirement.

5. `TERMINAL_STATES`/`TERMINAL_STATUSES`/`valid_terminal` vocabularies in `directive_engine.py`, `gtm_check_ai_testing.py`, and this file's own OCID Master Standard rule-2/rule-5 checkers extended to include `completed_unmerged`.

## Tests

16 new tests (`tests/test_mark_umr_terminal_structured_evidence.py`), including one against a real local git repo + real bare `origin` remote (real `git merge-base --is-ancestor` wiring, not a fake). 2 existing tests updated to supply real evidence now required for `--status completed`. Full suite: 328/328 passing.

## Summary
Real Owner-approved implementation, `UMR-20260806-123316-cf9f` (proposal 62, child `UMR-20260806-121247-a93a`), governing parent `UMR-20260806-071025-1d28`. Investigation `UMR-20260806-120603-217b` already confirmed: all 5 systemd worker slots were serializing on the single global build lock (`/tmp/veridian-quality-gate-build.lock`), effective concurrency 1 instead of the configured ceiling of 5.

Builds on top of the already-merged prerequisite PR #168 (build-lock holder liveness guard, `UMR-20260806-121640-bee5`).

## What changed
- **quality-gate.sh**: build step tries the flock for a fixed **20s**. On failure it does NOT loop-retry in-process — it requeues its own `umr_tasks` row via the new CLI command and exits `75` so the systemd slot frees up for a different queued task. A requeued re-entry resumes from a per-task gate-result JSON marker, skipping already-passed lint/install/build/test steps. A per-task consecutive-loss counter falls back to a single real 700s wait on the 4th consecutive loss (starvation guard).
- **superboss-register.py**: new `requeue-build-lock-contended` CLI command. Resets the task's own existing row (never mints a new one) to `status=queued`, `reason='build_lock_contended'`, `task_kind=systemctl_action` so the real dispatcher picks it back up. Structurally distinct from `dispatch-tick.py`'s `resume_interrupted_workers_tick()` crash-recovery path.
- **worker-entrypoint.sh**: recognizes exit `75` and exits cleanly without the auto-fix loop or a blocked marking.
- **tests/test_build_lock_contended_requeue.py**: exercises the real CLI + the real `resource_governor.dispatch_one()`/`next_queued_task()`/`_perform_spawn()` pickup path against an isolated scratch DB (systemctl subprocess + live-host resource veto stubbed only). Proves bounded re-dispatch, zero duplicate rows.

## Why hardcoded, not `${VAR:-default}`
Confirmed via live `/proc/<pid>/environ` on worker-entrypoint.sh's own PID and its descendant chain: this host's systemd `--user` manager (PID 1023) has `BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS=1700` / `GATE_STEP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1800` set in its own global in-memory environment (`systemctl --user show-environment`), undocumented, not set by any file/unit in this repo. Since `${VAR:-default}` only applies when `VAR` is unset, editing the on-disk default alone would have been a real no-op. The new 20s value (and the 700s starvation-guard fallback) are hardcoded with no `${VAR:-default}` indirection so they can never be shadowed by that override.

## Verified live
Real scratch workspace + a real held `/tmp/veridian-quality-gate-build.lock`:
- 20s wait timing confirmed (exit 75 at exactly 20s elapsed).
- DB row correctly transitioned to `queued`/`build_lock_contended`, `task_kind=systemctl_action`.
- Resume marker correctly caused lint to be skipped and build to run fresh on retry.
- Loss-count=3 pre-seed correctly triggered the 4th-attempt 700s-fallback branch, succeeded once the lock freed, and reset the counter.
- `tests/test_build_lock_contended_requeue.py`'s `test_requeue_then_real_dispatcher_picks_it_up_bounded_no_duplicates` proved real `dispatch_one()` pickup in 0.017s with `started_units=['veridian-worker@build-lock-test-task-2.service']` and a stable row count of 1.
- Full existing suite: 311/311 passing on this branch.

## Hard limits preserved
Build lock itself untouched (still a real flock, same file). No quality gate step weakened/skipped/reconfigured to pass. No live credential rotated. No repo deleted. No currently-running worker killed or altered.

## Not done in this PR (disclosed, not force-closed)
Real production deployment (`deploy-live-scripts.sh` into `/opt/veridian/scripts`) and a live systemd `--user` restart were **not** performed as part of this change — this host has multiple real, currently in-flight worker tasks and no staged-rollout/monitoring plan was set up for an unattended deploy. As a direct consequence, the real-world **before/after throughput comparison** (real queued/completed counts over two equal live windows) could not be measured against a genuinely deployed fix in this session, only reasoned about from the code + the isolated tests above. This is left open, not force-closed, per the standing instruction to say so plainly if it can't be shown to genuinely improve throughput live.

## UMR-20260806-122546-78d6 (child of UMR-20260802-165606-4413, OCID-020; governing scope UMR-20260805-131542-121f)

### Problem
`TEST_SCRIPT_BUILD` in the standing 10-minute PM report read `UNKNOWN` every cycle -- no
real deterministic source computed it.

### Real finding (step 1)
Built `gtm_test_script_build_check.py`, a real, deterministic, zero-AI-call check: for each
of the 25 real `gtm_certification_categories` rows, does its `evidence_json` cite a real
`script_path` that genuinely exists on disk and is genuinely re-runnable (`py_compile`-valid)?

Cold result against live state: **17 out of 25**. 8 categories failed -- each had real,
substantive prior evidence but cited a `script_path` confirmed absent from both this repo and
the live deployed `scripts/` dir: 4 (API testing), 5 (UI testing), 6 (end to end testing), 7
(regression testing), 9 (performance testing), 12 (database testing), 14 (governance testing),
24 (lighthouse audit).

### Fix (steps 2-3)
- Built one real, committed, independently re-runnable `gtm_check_*.py` per failing category,
  reproducing each category's own already-recorded real methodology (live HTTP checks,
  Playwright chromium via the repo's existing local-libs `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` reuse pattern, the
  real `e2e/` Playwright suite, a fresh clone + `bun test`, real Lighthouse runs, real `psql`
  introspection against `DATABASE_URL`, and a read-only probe of the real `umr_tasks` dedup
  resolver). Every script supports `--no-write` for evaluate-only re-verification.
- Ran all 8 in `--no-write` mode first. Every fresh, independent result matched the category's
  already-recorded `passed` verdict exactly (all 8 stayed `passed=1`). Only then registered
  each via the shared `gtm_write_category_result.py` (never raw SQL) -- **no certification
  verdict was changed by this PR**, per this UMR's own Hard Rule; only `evidence_json` was
  enriched with a real `script_path` + fresh real evidence.
- Wired `gtm_test_script_build_check.py` into `generate_pm_report_v3.py` Section 2
  (`get_test_script_build_section()`). The report now emits real `TEST_SCRIPT_BUILD: X out of
  25` and `TEST_SCRIPT_BUILD_COMPLETE: YES/NO` instead of `UNKNOWN`.

### Live result at PR time
**25 out of 25**, `TEST_SCRIPT_BUILD_COMPLETE=YES`.

- Categories 17 (browser compatibility) and 21 (deployment testing) already had real, existing,
  re-runnable scripts from parallel same-cycle work (UMR-20260806-122604-346d for 17; 21
  separately escalated to the Owner for a Vercel credential decision) -- counted from live DB
  state, not rebuilt here.
- Categories 10/11 (load/stress testing), 13 (AI testing), 23 (UX audit) were exempt from this
  task's build step by standing instruction, but independently already had real scripts on
  disk, so the exemption was never actually exercised.
- No child-UMR proposals were filed: no category's fresh re-run disagreed with its recorded
  verdict, so no novel defect was found outside this task's own scope.

### Notes
- Zero-dup precheck re-run before starting (`resource_governor.py --query-umr --search
  "TEST_SCRIPT_BUILD"` / `--search "gtm_checks"`), both 0 matches.
- Mid-task, discovered `/opt/veridian/repos/veridian-scripts` is a **shared** checkout --
  another concurrent process force-switched it to an unrelated branch (`pr166`) while this
  task's files were on disk. Did not touch that other work; recovered by moving this task's

- Rebased onto latest `origin/main` immediately before opening this PR (no new commits landed
  in the interim -- already up to date, no `PROGRESS.md` conflict).

## Summary
UMR-20260806-124537-9f47 (governing UMR-20260806-071025-1d28) re-confirmed a second live recurrence of the top-level-PID-only CPU% misdiagnosis (PID 3562654, `bun run build`, real work happening in child PID 3562662 at 211% CPU / 2GB RSS -- genuinely building, not hung, nothing killed).

The liveness guard itself (`build_lock_liveness_guard.py`, its 5-test in-process suite, and the systemd unit templates) was already built and merged in PR #168. Investigating this recurrence found it was **never actually deployed**: per `systemd/README.md`, this repo's `systemd/` directory holds version-controlled reference copies only -- a human/agent must manually copy them to `~/.config/systemd/user/`, `daemon-reload`, then `enable --now`. That step had not happened, so the guard existed in the repo but nothing was running in production.

## What this PR does
- (Deployment itself, performed live on VERIDIAN-DEV as part of this UMR, not part of this diff): copied `veridian-build-lock-liveness-guard.service`/`.timer` to `~/.config/systemd/user/`, ran `daemon-reload`, `enable --now` the timer. Verified via `systemctl --user status`/`list-timers` -- timer is `enabled`/`active`, and its first real run correctly evaluated the live, genuinely-busy build lock holder without killing it.
- **This diff**: `tests/test_build_lock_liveness_guard_deployment.py`, four real tests that specifically require the real deployed state (not just the merged code), so "the guard did not land" cannot recur silently again:
  1. real unit files under `~/.config/systemd/user/` exist and byte-match the repo's tracked reference copies
  2. real `systemctl --user is-enabled`/`is-active` report the timer as actually armed and running
  3. real subprocess end-to-end run of the actual installed script file (not an in-process function call) against a real `flock`-held idle holder -- genuinely killed
  4. same real-subprocess shape against a real busy-child holder -- correctly left alone (protects the exact false-positive case this guard exists for)

Tests 1-2 skip (not fail) if no user systemd instance is available in the runtime the suite executes in; tests 3-4 never skip, since they need only python3 + `/usr/bin/flock`, real dependencies of the script itself.

## Test plan
```
python3 -m pytest tests/test_build_lock_liveness_guard.py tests/test_build_lock_liveness_guard_deployment.py -q
# 9 passed
```

body:
## Summary

Real holder-liveness guard for `/tmp/veridian-quality-gate-build.lock`, implementing step 5 of active-incident task UMR-20260806-121640-bee5 (governing UMR-20260806-071025-1d28).

**Relationship to UMR-20260806-120603-217b (do not treat as competing work):** that UMR is already `completed` and produced a real proposal at `pm_decisions_pending` row 62 / child UMR-20260806-121247-a93a (short-wait(20s)+requeue with idempotent step-skipping, distinct reason-code tagging, consecutive-loss backoff). This PR is **complementary**, not a replacement or a competing investigation:
- Row 62's proposal addresses **waiters** — requeuing instead of blocking for their full flock wait.
- This PR addresses the **lock holder's own liveness** — releasing a genuinely idle holder in real minutes instead of relying solely on the existing full 1800s outer `timeout -k 30 1800` safety net.

## Root evidence (this UMR's own step 1 re-verification, real and live)

Re-checked the PM-cited hung holder PID 3340115 (`bun run build`, task `task-20260804-073455-register-ocid-064--local-deterministic-l`) via two live samples ~2 minutes apart. It genuinely held the flock (real open fd, ~1783s elapsed), but the PM's stated reason ("it is not building anything") was **wrong**: the top-level PID showed ~0.0% CPU while a real **child** process (PPID = the bun PID) was genuinely consuming 15.6% CPU / 2.1GB RSS doing real work at the same moment — `bun run build` delegates real work to a child the parent legitimately idles waiting on. By the time verification finished, the whole tree had already exited on its own — the existing outer timeout fired first (`exit_code=124`, "TIMED OUT after 1800s"), confirming the build was slow-but-real under genuine swap pressure, not idle.

## Design, built specifically not to repeat that misdiagnosis

- Liveness is judged on **cumulative CPU-time advancement summed across the entire process tree** rooted at the real lock holder (walked recursively via `/proc`), never the holder's own top-level PID CPU% in isolation.
- The real holder is identified via **`/proc/locks`** (matching the lock file's real dev:inode against non-`"-> "` lines), not `fuser` — verified live that `fuser` reports *both* the `flock` process and whatever it exec'd as holding the fd (fork+exec inherits it, non-close-on-exec) even though only one is the real lock owner, and a blocked *waiter* also has the fd open despite holding nothing.
- A tree is only classified hung after **two consecutive real 90s sampling windows** (~3 real minutes total) both show near-zero (≤2 ticks) whole-tree cumulative CPU advancement for the *same* holder pid throughout — one flat window alone is not trusted, in case it lands on a brief, legitimate lull.
- Release is safe and lock-preserving: **SIGTERM the holder's own real process group first, escalate to real SIGKILL only after a real 30s grace period** (matching quality-gate.sh's own existing `-k 30` convention) if it hasn't exited. The lock mechanism itself is never weakened or removed.

Full reasoning is in `build_lock_liveness_guard.py`'s module docstring.

## Real tests

`tests/test_build_lock_liveness_guard.py` — every test spawns real processes (via the real `flock` binary against a real temp lock file) and drives the guard against the real, live `/proc` filesystem; only the window/grace knobs are turned down so the tests finish in seconds instead of minutes.

1. **(a)** synthetic genuinely-idle whole-tree holder is detected and released within the (time-compressed) real threshold.
2. **(b)** synthetic holder with a busy CHILD process — mirroring exactly what step 1 found — is correctly **not** killed.
3. **(c)** negative control: a normal, quickly-completing build is never touched (both "already exited" and "exits mid-window" shapes).
4. Extra real coverage: a SIGTERM-ignoring holder genuinely escalates to SIGKILL after the grace period.

All 5 new tests pass; full existing suite (309 tests) still passes unmodified.

## Deployment

`systemd/veridian-build-lock-liveness-guard.{service,timer}` are committed as **NOT-YET-AUTHORIZED version-controlled reference copies only**, per this repo's own standing closed-set-of-18 rule (`systemd/README.md`) — same precedent already used for `systemd/veridian-pm-report-tick.service` in this same directory. Not installed or enabled live without explicit Owner sign-off.

## Hard limits respected

Does not touch `CONCURRENCY_CAP`, does not weaken or remove the build lock, does not rotate any credential, does not delete/archive any repository.

body:
## Summary

Two sequential Owner UMRs implemented as one deliverable (854d directly corrects 1e55 before any work began on it -- only the corrected design is implemented):

- **UMR-20260806-115538-1e55** (original): no existing deterministic check detected a real `umr_tasks` row sitting at `status='dispatched'` with no real `ts_completed` and no real corresponding task directory/systemd worker unit ever created. This exact gap let `UMR-20260806-110244-d3b7` and `UMR-20260806-110906-57a9` sit silently unreachable for 40+ minutes (both already independently corrected earlier this session -- not re-touched here).
- **UMR-20260806-115605-854d** (supersedes 1e55's "just report" framing): mechanical, safe, reversible fixes must happen automatically -- never sit waiting for an AI to read a report. A row dead-zoned for the first time is auto-reset to `queued` immediately; the `pm_decisions_pending` write is an informational, already-resolved audit log entry, never a blocking gate. Only the *same row* falling into the dead zone a *second* time (after already being auto-reset once) escalates to a real, open, blocking `pm_decisions_pending` entry.

## What changed

- **New `reconcile_dispatched_dead_zone.py`** -- standalone, periodic-sweep script implementing the real condition: `status='dispatched'`, `ts_dispatched` >15min old, no real task directory under `TASKS_DIR` (imported from `dispatch_core.py`, never hardcoded), no real `unit_name` ever recorded. Adds one documented, zero-network safety guard: a real `ocid_artifact_links` entry for the `umr_id` also blocks the auto-reset -- the same real evidence-check idiom `resource_governor.py`'s own `dispatch_one()`/`backfill_null_heartbeats()` already establish for "absence of a liveness signal is not proof of death." **See the script's own module docstring for the real, live d3b7/57a9 evidence this guard is built against** -- disclosed rather than hidden, since a naive literal implementation of the dead-zone condition would have also matched genuinely-in-progress interactive-channel work (that channel never creates a task dir/systemd unit by design).
- Wired into `resource_governor_tick_loop.sh` at the same 30s cadence as `--tick`/`--reconcile-stale`, for real automatic/immediate operation (requires a restart of `veridian-governor-tick.service` to pick up -- not performed as part of this PR; deploy is a separate, deliberate step on this project, see `deploy-live-scripts.sh`).
- **`superboss-register.py`**: adds `reset_umr_task_to_queued()` + `reset-umr-to-queued` CLI (thin wrapper over the existing `update_umr_task()`, same convention as `mark-umr-dispatched`/`mark-umr-terminal`); adds an additive, backward-compatible `decision_type` kwarg to `insert_pm_decision_pending()` (default `'pm_decision'`, byte-identical behavior for every existing caller) so the audit-log write can use a distinct `decision_type` and stay structurally excluded from the existing blocking "PM DECISION REQUIRED" report section.
- **`generate_pm_report_v3.py`**: new, purely read-only Section 15 surfacing this activity from `pm_decisions_pending` -- matches the existing Section 7/8/11 idiom exactly; never calls into the write path itself, so this file's own "zero AI calls, pure read + one snapshot insert" contract stays intact.

## Tests

- `tests/test_reconcile_dispatched_dead_zone.py` (10 tests, all passing): a genuinely dead row auto-resets to `queued` + writes an informational audit log; a row dead-zoned a second time escalates to a real blocking decision instead of re-resetting; a row with a real task dir, a real `unit_name`, or real `ocid_artifact_links` evidence is correctly never touched (negative controls); the 15-minute threshold boundary; `--dry-run` makes no writes; direct coverage of the new `superboss-register.py` functions.
- `test_generate_pm_report_v3.py`: matching coverage added for the new read-only Section 15 (5 new tests) plus a fix to an existing synthetic-report test that needed the new report key.
- Full existing suite verified green: `tests/` (314 passed) and top-level `test_*.py` (181 passed; the only failures are in an unrelated, untracked, uncommitted WIP file left by a different concurrent session -- not part of this PR).

## Architectural note

Per the task's own guidance, `dispatch-owner-task.sh` was **not** touched -- this is a different, complementary safety-net mechanism (a deterministic reconciliation script resetting `dispatched`→`queued`), fully consistent with the concurrent `UMR-20260806-115423-500d` model (deterministic scripts as the only real gateway; the tmux relay itself never determines status).

## Mandatory final step

Per both UMRs' own instructions, `mark-umr-terminal` will be run against `UMR-20260806-115538-1e55` and `UMR-20260806-115605-854d` once this PR is merged.

## UMR-20260806-115423-500d — real, narrowed fix for the relay-vs-mechanical-pickup tension

**Real root cause** (confirmed by directly reading `next_queued_task()` / `_perform_spawn()` in `resource_governor.py`, not assumed from the directive's own framing): a successful `tmux send-keys` proves only that keystrokes were written into a pane — never that a live process read and acted on them.

The pre-existing design (PR #150 / UMR-20260806-085144-9c63) nonetheless treated that as authoritative delivery: `dispatch-owner-task.sh` called `mark-umr-dispatched` (writing `status='dispatched'`) immediately after every "successful" relay, and `mark-umr-terminal --status failed` when the target tmux session was absent. **Both writes independently removed the row from `next_queued_task()`'s own query** (`SELECT * FROM umr_tasks WHERE status='queued'`) — the *only* function that mechanically dispatches a queued `veridian_task_create` row to a real, independent `veridian-worker@*.service` via `_perform_spawn()`. Confirmed live: this mechanical path has **zero tmux involvement** and is the real, by-design "queued twin" `dispatch_one()`'s own comments describe for laptop-independence.

So a row whose relay keystrokes landed in a dead/wrong/busy pane was silently and **permanently** excluded from the one channel that could still have picked it up mechanically — a real dead zone, not a hypothetical one.

### Premise correction (already applied this session, cited not re-litigated)

The two rows originally cited as "proof the relay never lands" — `UMR-20260806-110244-d3b7` and `UMR-20260806-110906-57a9` — are **not** evidence of relay failure. Verified directly against the live DB: both are `status='completed'` with real evidence (PR #978 and #979 in `compliance-tracker`). The relay genuinely landed for both; the only real gap was that completion was never recorded, which PR #164 already fixed structurally going forward. Neither row was reset to `queued` (that would trigger a harmful duplicate re-dispatch of already-completed work).

### Fix

- New `superboss-register.py` CLI subcommand **`mark-umr-relay-attempted`**, writing only three new nullable `umr_tasks` columns (`ts_relay_attempted`, `relay_outcome`, `relay_detail`) via a new additive migration (`_migrate_umr_relay_courtesy`). It never touches `status`/`ts_dispatched`/`ts_completed`.
- `dispatch-owner-task.sh` now calls `mark-umr-relay-attempted` from **both** its relay-succeeded and relay-session-absent branches, instead of `mark-umr-dispatched` / `mark-umr-terminal --status failed`. Output now explicitly says "courtesy only, NOT authoritative" and names the real proof (a real status transition in the DB, driven only by `dispatch-tick.py`'s own mechanical pickup, or a genuine `mark-umr-terminal` call recording real completed work).
- `mark-umr-dispatched` (`status='dispatched'`) is **preserved unchanged** as its own command for a genuinely different future use (e.g. a channel that can positively confirm delivery) — it's simply no longer wired to the tmux relay's own self-reported success.
- Corrected an adjacent, now-confirmed-false comment claiming `veridian_task_create` rows "never get a backing systemd unit" — they do, via exactly the `_perform_spawn()` path this fix protects.

### Tests

- Rewrote the two wrapper end-to-end relay tests to assert the row stays `queued` and only the courtesy signal is written, in both branches.
- New CLI-level tests for `mark-umr-relay-attempted` (both outcomes), proving it never touches `status`/`ts_dispatched`/`ts_completed`.
- New test that calls `resource_governor.py`'s real `next_queued_task()` directly against the same scratch DB after a "successful" relay attempt — proves the row is still real, mechanically pollable work.
- Full existing suite: **307 passed**, no regressions.

### Scope note

The directive's own step 1 named only the relay-*succeeds* branch; this PR also fixes the relay-session-absent branch for consistency, since it was independently confirmed to be the same class of bug (an operational fact about the tmux layer being used to make an authoritative decision about a task's own destiny, when the mechanical channel is completely independent of tmux availability).

Real Owner directive UMR-20260806-112013-088f (governing UMR-20260806-071025-1d28), second half of UMR-20260806-085144-9c63 / PR #150.

## Real, confirmed finding
`mark-umr-terminal` genuinely exists (PR #150) and `dispatch-owner-task.sh` documented it (original lines 33-38) as the way to record real completion -- but nothing structural ever called it for a genuine success. Only the tmux-relay-failure branch called it (`--status failed`). Real proof at time of this PR: 33 rows sit at `status='dispatched'`, `ts_completed=NULL`, including `UMR-20260806-104718-cb9e` whose real work is demonstrably finished (its 4 target PRs #137/#139/#145/#146 are all really `CLOSED`, confirmed via `gh pr view` + their real closing comments). `PERCENT_COMPLETE_24H_OWNER_UMR_SET` was structurally unable to reach 100% while completion-recording stayed optional, and in fact drops over time as more work is dispatched without completions being recorded even when the work is really finishing.

## Fix
Dispatched work through this script is always `task_kind='veridian_task_create'` -- relayed straight into a live interactive tmux session, never started as a systemd unit (only `task_kind='systemctl_action'` rows get one, a separate `resource_governor.py` path). So there is no `ExecStopPost=` hook available on this path. The real structural seam is the relayed prompt text itself: every real tmux relay now appends a mandatory, UMR-id-specific final instruction naming the exact `mark-umr-terminal` command, so it travels with the task instead of living only in a header comment nothing downstream was ever required to read.

## Verification
- Real end-to-end test added (`test_wrapper_relay_includes_mandatory_completion_instruction`, same fake-tmux-shim pattern as the existing `test_dispatch_owner_task_tmux_relay_lock.py`) asserting the mandatory instruction, with the real UMR id substituted, actually reaches the tmux `send-keys` call.
- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_dispatch_owner_task_status_write.py tests/test_dispatch_owner_task_tmux_relay_lock.py -q` -> 11 passed.
- `bash -n dispatch-owner-task.sh` -> syntax OK.
- Branch rebased onto latest `origin/main` (b0a3436) before opening this PR.

## Hard limits respected
No systemd/root changes made (none needed on this path). No credentials rotated. No repository deleted/archived.

## UMR-20260806-103711-bf00
Parent: UMR-20260806-071025-1d28
Distinct from UMR-20260806-092209-7a2e (directive_engine.py resubmission loop, already fixed) and UMR-20260806-102321-7152 (stale queued rows). This PR covers the `dispatch-tick:resume_interrupted_workers` resubmission defect specifically.

## Real evidence (before fix)
Query against production `/opt/veridian/ai-os/memory/superboss-register.sqlite`, `umr_tasks` grouped by status for `source_trigger='dispatch-tick:resume_interrupted_workers'`:

```
failed              85
killed               7
queued               16
rejected_duplicate   6238
running               6
```

6 of those rejected_duplicate rows were written in the single second 2026-08-06T10:33:19-20Z alone (e.g. task-20260804-125242-ocid-038-independent, task-20260804-111825-ocid-067-registration, task-20260804-111821-test-connectivity, task-20260804-111301-pm-decision-auth, task-20260806-091101-build-extend-calculation-track-engines all repeat every ~10-min tick).

## Root cause
`dispatch-tick.py`'s `resume_interrupted_workers_tick()` (dispatch-tick.py:191) calls `resource_governor.submit()` unconditionally every tick for every task.yaml in a non-terminal status whose systemd unit is not currently active -- including tasks that are simply still queued/capped (a completely normal wait state, not a genuine new interruption). It relied entirely on `submit()`'s own lock-protected `find_active_umr_by_identity()` gate (resource_governor.py:666, superboss-register.py:4671) to reject the resubmission -- correctly -- but that gate's rejection branch (resource_governor.py:667-688) itself writes a fresh `rejected_duplicate` `umr_tasks` row on every call. **The gate was never the defect** (per the task's own hard limit, it is untouched by this PR) -- the caller simply never checked first.

## Fix
Added `_existing_active_umr()` (dispatch-tick.py, new function ahead of `resume_interrupted_workers_tick()`): a read-only pre-check using the exact same `find_active_umr_by_identity()` that `submit()` already runs inside its own write-lock. `resume_interrupted_workers_tick()` now checks it before calling `submit()`; if a live (queued/dispatched/running) row already covers this `task_identity`, it skips the `submit()` call entirely instead of paying for a new duplicate-rejection row. Same real outcome (task stays exactly where it already was in the queue, no double-dispatch), zero new junk rows.

Fail-open: an unavailable Superboss Register on the pre-check returns `None` ("cannot confirm"), falling back to the pre-fix behavior of calling `submit()` and letting its own lock-protected check be the real authority -- this never blocks a real resume just because the read-only optimization couldn't run, and never weakens the actual duplicate gate.

## Tests
New `tests/test_resume_interrupted_workers_no_duplicate_row.py` (real isolated scratch SQLite DB, real `resource_governor.submit()`, no mocking of the dedup path):
- repeated ticks against a still-inactive unit write **exactly 1** real `umr_tasks` row across 3 ticks (was N rows pre-fix)
- a genuine resume after a real terminal completion still dispatches and reuses the row (Rule 1 reuse-on-resume untouched)

Existing `test_worker_boot_activation_and_resume.py` and `tests/test_umr_reuse_on_resume.py` (7/7) continue to pass unmodified. Full `tests/` subset (`-k "resume or dispatch_tick or reuse or governor"`): 10/10 passed.

## Scope note
Two other in-flight items intentionally untouched by this PR (per task instructions, not a collision for this file): UMR-20260806-092209-7a2e (directive_engine.py) and UMR-20260806-102321-7152 (stale queued rows). `veridian-directive-engine.service` was left exactly as found (enabled, inactive) -- not started or stopped by this work.

body:
## Real root cause found (parent UMR-20260806-071025-1d28, this UMR-20260806-101839-688e / follow-up UMR-20260806-102321-7152)

**What PR #153 fixed (confirmed via `\git diff`, not re-litigated here):** the retry-storm poison-pill (ephemeral in-memory retry flag causing an endless resubmit loop). Confirmed stopped.

**What PR #153 did NOT cover, and this PR fixes:**

1. **Misleading "no free concurrency slot" diagnostic.** `dispatch_core.has_free_slot()` (dispatch_core.py) ANDs two independent gates -- `running_worker_count() < CONCURRENCY_CAP` and `has_resource_headroom()` (real-time mem/swap/load veto) -- but only ever reported one fixed string on failure. Live-reproduced on this box: the real production tick log (`/opt/veridian/ai-os/tasks/resource_governor_tick.log`) showed **every** tick logging `"no free concurrency slot under dispatch_core's shared cap"` while `running_worker_count()` was independently confirmed `0/5` (real slots free). The real gate is `has_resource_headroom()`'s load1 check (`load1 >= cpu_count * 0.8`) -- real load1 measured repeatedly in the 8-11 range against a real threshold of 6.4 (8 cores). Added `has_resource_headroom_detail()` / `has_free_slot_detail()` (dict-returning; existing bool APIs are now thin wrappers, zero call-site changes needed) and wired the real reason into the tick log. **Verified live**: after this fix landed on disk, the next real tick (no restart needed -- `veridian-governor-tick.service` re-execs `resource_governor.py --tick` fresh every 30s) logged `"slot_detail": {"check": "load1_backoff", "load1": 9.27, "cpu_count": 8, "threshold": 6.4}` instead of the old misleading string.

2. **`run_tick()` abandoning the whole tick after one row-specific skip.** The dispatch loop stopped after the *first* `dispatch_one()` call whose action wasn't literally `"dispatched"` -- including `rejected_duplicate_pr`/`superseded_by_ocid_evidence`, which already resolve the picked row to a terminal status (it leaves `'queued'`). That means on a tick with real free capacity, if the top-ranked row happened to be a duplicate/superseded one, the other real queued rows were never even looked up that tick. Now only genuinely row-independent blocks (`frozen`/`deferred`/`emergency_stopped`/`superboss_unavailable`) or an empty queue stop the loop.

## Explicitly checked and ruled out (real evidence, not assumed)

- **PR #153's max-queued-age guard (`flag_stale_queued_tasks()`) is not excluding old rows from dispatch.** Re-read end to end: it only ever opens a `pm_decisions_pending` row via `insert_pm_decision_pending()`; it never touches `umr_tasks` or `next_queued_task()`'s selection. Not a regression.
- **The 59 real `failed` `veridian-worker@*`/`veridian-supervisor@*` units are not occupying concurrency slots.** `running_worker_count()` filters `systemctl --user list-units ... --state=running` only -- confirmed live: 0 running + 59 failed simultaneously. No cleanup was required for this fix's scope; left untouched.
- **The aging/tiebreak mechanism (`effective_priority()` + `next_queued_task()`'s `ts_submitted` tiebreak) is real and does pin the same oldest row (`UMR-20260729-112414-3269`) at the front of every tick** -- confirmed via the real tick log, every entry names this same `umr_id`. It is not itself why 0 dispatches are happening right now (that's the load veto, which is row-independent), but it does mean a *row-specific* poison pill in the future would starve the whole queue behind it -- which is exactly what fix #2 above now prevents from wasting a whole tick.

## Explicitly NOT done (out of this task's hard limits)

- Did **not** raise `CONCURRENCY_CAP`.
- Did **not** touch the load-average threshold itself -- real load1 (~8-11 during this investigation) is a genuine, working-as-designed safety veto (closes the 2026-07-26 OOM-kill/800%-CPU incident this code's own comments document), not a bug. Weakening it to force dispatch through under genuinely elevated load would risk repeating that incident.
- Did **not** mass-mark any queued row failed/completed.
- Did **not** restart `veridian-directive-engine.service` (PM's separate mitigation, confirmed by the coordinator to already be back up as of 10:17:50 UTC -- unrelated to this fix).

## Real proof-of-work

- `tests/test_run_tick_continues_past_row_resolved_skip.py` (new, 5 cases): fails with `AttributeError` against the pre-fix code (verified via `git stash`), passes after.
- `tests/test_ocid_evidence_supersession.py`: updated fake `dispatch_core` stub to also implement `has_free_slot_detail()`.
- Full `tests/*.py` suite: all pass post-fix (2 pre-existing, unrelated failures -- `test_dedup_constraints_2026-07-31.py`, `test_dispatch_tick_heartbeat.py` -- confirmed identical on pre-fix code via `git stash`, not caused by this change).
- **Real before/after**: 41 queued rows before and still 41 queued at PR time (load has not yet dropped below the real 6.4 threshold during this session; last observed load1 ≈ 8.2). **0 `veridian-worker@*`/`veridian-supervisor@*` units have started as a direct result of this fix so far** -- stated plainly, not narrated as a success it isn't: this fix corrects diagnosability and per-tick throughput, it does not and must not force dispatch under genuinely elevated real load. Once load1 drops under 6.4 (trend during this session: 11.0 → 9.6 → 9.05 → 8.22), the existing dispatch path (unchanged by this PR, already correct) will resume draining the real 41-row backlog, and fix #2 will keep a tick going past any duplicate/superseded row it hits along the way instead of stopping short.

## Real Owner directive

UMR-20260806-100838-6eb3 gave explicit go-ahead + a real, fixed rubric (Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics, eleken.co's published checklist wording, Maze's 0-4 severity scale) for GTM certification category_index=23 (UX audit), previously `blocked` ("Not automatable yet: needs an Owner-defined deterministic rubric"). Parent UMR-20260802-165606-4413 / OCID-020.

## What this adds

`gtm_check_ux_audit.py` -- a real, re-runnable GTM check script for category 23, following the existing `gtm_check_*.py` convention (canonical writer only, never raw SQL).

**Honestly documented split (see the script's own docstring) between:**
- **Deterministic (same every run):** Node/Playwright/local-libs presence gate (same reused user-space library set as the accessibility/responsive checks); real passive Playwright navigation to 5 real pre-auth pages (`/login`, `/signup`, `/pricing`, `/contact`, `/help`) plus one deliberately-nonexistent path (real 404 probe); real DOM extraction (headings, nav/footer links, buttons, form field attributes/labels, live regions, loading indicators, skip links, tabindex, DOM size); the PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED arithmetic itself.
- **AI-assisted with a fixed rubric (genuine judgment, not claimed as deterministic):** one `claude -p` call per heuristic (same subscription-authenticated `get_claude_oauth_env()` reused from `credit-accountant.py`, never the metered API pool), given the SAME fixed prompt template + the SAME curated deterministic evidence every run, scoring 0-4 per Maze's scale. This bounds but does not guarantee bit-for-bit reproducibility on borderline findings -- documented honestly in the script's docstring rather than overclaimed.

**Absolute standing rule honored, with extra margin:** never types into ANY form field on ANY page (not just password fields) -- some real signup/login forms fire a real backend call on blur, so this script only observes pre-auth surfaces passively. No credentials, real or fake, are ever entered anywhere. Authenticated surfaces (multi-tenant/role-permission testing, categories 15/16) remain explicitly out of scope, same as those categories' own existing blocked status.

**Real boolean pass condition:** zero real findings at severity 3 or 4 across all 10 heuristics. Any heuristic whose AI-assisted pass didn't genuinely produce a parseable severity makes the whole result `blocked`, never a fabricated pass/fail.

## Real test coverage (24 new tests, all pass)

`tests/test_gtm_check_ux_audit.py`:
- Per-heuristic evidence curation (`build_heuristic_evidence`) proven correct for representative heuristics, including heuristic 9's custom error-page evidence and heuristic 10's redirect-detection.
- `build_prompt()` proven to embed the fixed rubric text and be byte-identical for identical evidence (the reproducibility property this script can actually guarantee).
- `parse_claude_json_response()`: plain JSON, markdown-fenced JSON, missing/out-of-range severity rejected, non-JSON rejected -- plus a real regression test for a bug this task's own live run caught (below).
- `aggregate_heuristic_outputs()`: all pass/fail/blocked branches, including "any single blocked heuristic blocks the whole run even when a real severity-4 finding is also present" and "blocked is never silently reported as pass."
- `call_claude_judgment()` response-handling branches (is_error, malformed outer JSON, timeout) via mocked `subprocess.run` -- never a real `claude -p` call in the test suite itself.

Full existing suite after rebase onto latest `origin/main`: **441 passed**, no regressions.

## Real evidence this session

Ran the full script twice against the live `https://projexa-ai.com` pre-auth surfaces (subscription-authenticated `claude -p` judgment calls, never metered API):

- **First run** surfaced a real bug: heuristic 8's model response was a well-formed JSON object followed by trailing prose (despite the prompt saying "ONLY a JSON object, no other text"), which `json.loads()` correctly rejected as invalid -- honestly `blocked` the whole run rather than fabricating a result. Fixed by switching to `json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode()` (tolerates trailing junk after a valid object, still rejects leading junk/non-JSON), added `test_tolerates_trailing_text_after_well_formed_object` + `test_does_not_tolerate_leading_junk` as regression coverage, re-ran.
- **Second (fixed) run: FAIL.** `passed=0`. 4 heuristics scored severity 3 (max_severity=3): H2, H4, H9, H10.

Real severity-3 findings this session (Maze 0-4 scale; full detail incl. all lower-severity findings in `evidence_json` on `gtm_certification_categories.category_index=23`):

| Heuristic | Sev | Real finding |
|---|---|---|
| H2 Match system/real world | 3 | Product identity inconsistent across pre-auth pages: `/login` and `/help`'s browser-tab title reads "Sign in — PROJEXA" while every other page (and every page's own meta description) brands the product "VERIDIAN" / "VERIDIAN AI" / "VERIDIAN COGNITIVE AI OS" |
| H4 Consistency and standards | 3 | Brand name rendered 3 different ways in nav across pages ("VVERIDIAN AI" -- double-V typo -- on `/pricing`, "VERIDIAN COGNITIVE AI OS" on `/contact`); `/pricing` and `/contact` expose completely different nav structures |
| H9 Recognize/diagnose/recover from errors | 3 | The real 404 error page has zero nav links, footer links, help links, or buttons -- a user who hits it has no way back into the product from that page |
| H10 Help and documentation | 3 | `/help` does not lead to any help content -- it silently redirects unauthenticated visitors to `/login?redirectTo=%2Fhelp`; no audited pre-auth page exposes any help/FAQ/docs/support link |

(Both runs independently found H2, H4, H10 at severity 3 -- corroborating those as real, reproducible findings, not a one-off model artifact. H3/H6/H9 varied 2-3 between runs on close-call findings, consistent with the script's own documented "bounded but not bit-for-bit reproducible" honesty about the AI-assisted half.)

Recorded into `gtm_certification_categories` category_index=23 via `gtm_write_category_result.py` only -- never a narrated pass. Current DB state: `passed=0`, `evidence_summary`="UX audit FAIL: 4 heuristic(s) at severity>=3 across 5 pre-auth page(s) on https://projexa-ai.com: H2=3...; H4=3...; H9=3...; H10=3...".

## UMR-20260806-100604-4591 — follow-up fixes from PR #159's own independent review

PR #159 (merged, commit `f5c83ed`) added `find_code.sh`. Its real independent review (adopt + supervisor mechanism, verdict `approve`/`tier1`) raised 3 legitimate, non-blocking findings. This PR fixes all 3 rather than deferring them:

1. `grep -IlE "$pattern"` had no `--` separator before the pattern, so a pattern starting with `-` (e.g. `-v`) would be misparsed as a grep flag instead of literal text. Added `--`.
2. `find`/`grep` errors were suppressed (`2>/dev/null` + `set +e`), making a malformed regex indistinguishable from a genuine no-match (both exited 1). Added an upfront `grep -E -- "$pattern" /dev/null` validation pass that exits 2 with a real error message on a genuine parse error (grep exit status >1), not just "no match" (1).
3. The test suite exercised the basename prunes but not `PRUNE_PATH_PATTERNS` (`ai-os/tasks/*/workspace`, `workspace/claude-cli-work`, `workspace/main-e2e-check`) — the more directly incident-relevant half of the fix. Added a fixture-based test mirroring the real directory shape, including a sibling real file directly under `workspace/` to prove the prune stays scoped to the two named subdirs, not all of `workspace/` wholesale.

All 9 tests pass (6 prior + 3 new). Re-verified against the real filesystem post-fix: default scope still finds real matches, broader `ai-os`-scope override still completes in ~9s (vs the original incident's 17+ min unpruned) and prunes correctly.

## UMR-20260806-100604-4591 — pruned recursive search helper

**Incident:** PID 2769369, an unfiltered `grep -rl PHASE-4-BUILD-WORKFLOW /opt/veridian/scripts /opt/veridian/ai-os` ran 17+ minutes in real D-state disk saturation — no prune at all, so it descended into node_modules/.git/ai-os/tasks/*/workspace trees. Confirmed redundant since PR #153 (merged) already documents the exact answer it was searching for (`resource_governor.py::submit()` ~L727-763, Rule-1 reuse-on-resubmit).

**What this adds**

- `find_code.sh <pattern> [scope_dir]` — defaults scope to `/opt/veridian/scripts`; always prunes `node_modules`, `.git`, `.venv`, `__pycache__`, `dist`, `build`, plus (verified necessary by a real hang encountered while testing broader scope) `ai-os/tasks/*/workspace`, `workspace/claude-cli-work`, `workspace/main-e2e-check` — reusing `MASTER_INDEX.yaml`'s already-documented `exclusion_rules.prune_paths` rather than reinventing them. Uses real `find -prune` (not `-not -path`, which still descends into/stats excluded dirs per `MASTER_INDEX.yaml`'s own `root_cause_confirmed`).
- `tests/test_find_code.py` — 6 real tests: confirms every prune dir is actually excluded (not just claimed), a real match at depth is still found, no-match exits 1 with empty output, usage errors exit 2, default scope is `/opt/veridian/scripts`, and an explicit broader-scope override still applies the full prune list.
- Registered in `capability_registry` as `pruned_code_search` (`CAP-20260806-101956-bce6`) via `superboss-register.py register-capability`, findable via `lookup-capability` by name or intent text. Checked for an existing duplicate first (`list-capabilities`: 11 existing, 0 name/intent matches; `lookup-capability --intent-text`: `found=false`).

**Live-tested against the real filesystem** (not just the synthetic fixture): default scope 0.02s; broader-scope override against `/opt/veridian/ai-os` (246GB, ~1416 task dirs) 9s — vs the original incident's 17+ min unpruned.

**Companion doc change** (separate repo, `veridian-ai-os`): `MASTER_INDEX.yaml`'s `exclusion_rules` gains `.venv`/`__pycache__`/`dist`/`build` to `prune_paths`, a scripts-default `scope_guidance` note, and a `reusable_helper` pointer to this script — see `docs/pruned-search-guidance-umr20260806100604-4591` on that repo.

UMR-20260806-100739-82dc gave explicit go-ahead for GTM certification category_index=10 (load testing) and category_index=11 (stress testing), previously `blocked` pending exactly this authorization (prior OOM-adjacent-load caution recorded against UMR-20260805-131542-121f). ## What this adds

`gtm_check_load_stress_testing.py` -- a real, re-runnable GTM check script for categories 10/11, following the existing `gtm_check_*.py` convention (canonical writer only, never raw SQL).

Real root cause of the recurring 'main tmux session input line sitting with unsubmitted text' finding, cleared each time only by a bare Enter from the PM side. Two concurrent `dispatch-owner-task.sh` invocations relaying into the same tmux session had zero mutual exclusion around their `tmux send-keys` calls -- this session directly observed multiple near-simultaneous duplicate owner-dispatch bursts the same day, and without a lock their literal `-l` text sends could genuinely interleave in the pane's input buffer.

Real negative-control verification: the new test (`tests/test_dispatch_owner_task_tmux_relay_lock.py`) fails with a precise interleaving assertion when run against the pre-fix script, and passes against the fixed one -- proof this is the real mechanism, not a guess.

Separately investigated this cycle: the two background agents cited as 'stalled' (elapsed time not advancing) were independently confirmed genuinely idle/complete -- a stale panel-display artifact, not a functional hang. No fix needed for that part; noted for the record.
