## UMR-20260806-091345-d90c (child of UMR-20260806-071025-1d28)

Deterministic 4-bucket triage of the trailing-24h `owner_dispatch_gateway`
`failed`/`killed` backlog.

### What this does

Recomputes the trailing-24h `owner_dispatch_gateway` `umr_tasks` set fresh
from the live DB every run -- no hardcoded counts. For every row with
`status IN ('failed','killed')`, cross-references real evidence:

- real `task.yaml` under `/opt/veridian/ai-os/tasks/<task_id>/` (derived
  from `unit_name`)
- real git/GitHub PR state for any repo/PR cited (`veridian-scripts`,
  `compliance-tracker`)
- the row's own real `reason`/`metadata_json` columns, already populated
  with structured evidence by this project's prior reconciliation passes

...and classifies into **exactly one** of:

1. **already_done** -- real work landed elsewhere; row status is stale.
   Requires a real `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main`
   confirmation -- never GitHub's `mergedAt` field alone.
2. **superseded** -- a later real row (same `task_identity`, later
   `ts_submitted`, non-terminal-failure status) covers the same goal.
   Deterministic tie-break: max `ts_submitted` among candidates.
3. **retryable** -- real mechanical failure cause (merge conflict,
   quality-gate failure, transient worker death with no task.yaml/PR ever
   created), no remaining blocker.
4. **blocked** -- real external blocker (credit-accountant rejection, the
   missing-reviewer-identity gap already confirmed real and repo-wide on
   compliance-tracker this session -- OCID-070, `UMR-20260805-034917-33a9`
   -- or a genuine Owner-only decision), **or** the deterministic fallback
   when no bucket-1/2/3 evidence is found (never guessed into a more
   convenient bucket).

Reproducibility: classification depends only on the row's own real DB
columns, task.yaml, and git/GitHub state -- never wall-clock-relative
"recency". A second run over an unchanged row returns the same bucket.

### Write path

Writes back **only** through `superboss-register.py`'s own
`update_umr_task()` inside its own `_write_lock()` (same convention as
`reconcile_owner_dispatch_status.py`, PR #147, now merged) -- read-existing
metadata / merge / write-back, never a blind replace, never raw SQL.

### Relationship to PR #147 (merged)

PR #147's `reconcile_owner_dispatch_status.py` reconciles stale
`status='running'` rows. This script covers the disjoint `failed`/`killed`
subset that PR #147 explicitly left out of scope. Reuses its
task.yaml-read / systemd-lookup / `update_umr_task()`-only convention.

### Per the standing propose-then-approve-then-execute mandate

This script implements **no fix** for bucket-3/4 rows itself.
`--file-proposals` (requires `--apply`) deposits one real child-UMR
proposal per bucket-3/4 row via the canonical `insert-owner-proposal` CLI
only -- issue = the real problem, proposal = the real proposed fix.
**Never** calls `decide-owner-proposal` -- propose only, no
auto-approve/execute.

### Real dry run against the live DB (report-only, no writes)

```
Trailing-24h owner_dispatch_gateway total (all statuses, recomputed fresh): 141
failed+killed rows triaged: 58
  already_done: 15
  superseded: 1
  retryable: 33
  blocked: 9
bucket sum: 58 (matches triaged total: True)
```

### Tests

25 new unit tests in `test_triage_owner_umr_24h.py`: `classify()`'s full
decision tree / priority order / determinism (including a property test
that every classification lands in exactly the 4 declared buckets),
`gather_evidence()`'s real regex/DB-query signal extraction (mocked
git/gh/task.yaml), the `update_umr_task()`-only write path (with a raising
stub proving no raw SQL write and existing-metadata-key preservation), and
`load_rows()`'s status/source_trigger filter. `python3 -m pytest -q` run
clean (25 passed); full-suite run also clean except 6 pre-existing,
unrelated failures in `test_dispatch_tick_heartbeat.py` (untracked file,
not touched by this PR, references a `dispatch_tick` module attribute that
doesn't currently exist -- confirmed pre-existing via `git status`, not
introduced here).

opening this PR; no `PROGRESS.md` conflict.

body:
## Real Owner directive
UMR-20260806-090229-f2a7 (dispatch-queue-starvation investigation), parent UMR-20260806-071025-1d28.

**Correction to the dispatch's premise (already independently verified before this work)**: the 3 "stuck" priority-1 UMRs cited in the original directive were all completed directly by the interactive executor this session, not via the systemd worker-dispatch queue — not good examples of the starvation bug. The core finding (30 real tier-1 rows stuck ~2 real days) is real and independently reconfirmed here with better, precisely-traced examples.

## Real root cause (confirmed live against production, not inferred)

`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM umr_tasks WHERE tier=1 AND status='queued'` = 30 at investigation start (`superboss-register.py`'s own `_connect()`), oldest dated `2026-08-04T00:03:34Z`.

The journalctl line the parent UMR cites (`[PHASE-3-BUILD-CALC]: check-duplicate battery call failed, fail-open, proceeding: Expecting value...`) is real but a **different, unrelated** mechanism than the PM's "silently requeued forever" theory: `run_check_duplicate_battery()` only runs for a task_identity with **no** existing `umr_tasks` row yet (`directive_engine.py` `process_one()` returns early for any row already `queued/dispatched/running`), and "fail-open" there just means the dup-check battery is skipped, not that anything loops.

The **real** mechanism, traced through real code + real live DB queries:

1. `directive_engine.py::process_one()` (old code) gated its "retry exactly once, then hold for Owner review" policy on `entry.get("_retried")` — an in-memory flag on a dict that `main()`'s own `directive = load_directive()` recreates fresh from `DIRECTIVE.yaml` every outer-loop tick (every `poll_seconds`, default 60s). That flag never survived to the next tick, so a chronically-failing `task_identity` was resubmitted on literally every tick, forever.

   Confirmed live: `task_identity` `PHASE-3-BUILD-CALC`/`PHASE-4-BUILD-WORKFLOW` (`DIRECTIVE.yaml` lines 194/205) resubmitted 20+ times since 2026-07-29 (`SELECT * FROM umr_tasks WHERE task_identity IN ('PHASE-3-BUILD-CALC','PHASE-4-BUILD-WORKFLOW')`).

2. Each later resubmission reused the same `umr_id` (`resource_governor.py::submit()`, lines 727-763, Rule-1 reuse-on-resubmit), and `superboss-register.py::upsert_umr_task()`'s `ON CONFLICT(umr_id) DO UPDATE` (lines 5236-5242) deliberately never refreshes `ts_submitted`. `UMR-20260730-181923-f2cd` kept `ts_submitted=2026-07-30T18:19:23` across every later resubmission.

3. `effective_priority()`/`next_queued_task()` (lines 794-810, confirmed via a live query against the real DB): a row idle long enough ages to `TIER_MIN=0`, tiebreak is ascending `ts_submitted`. The permanently-ancient-timestamped row therefore permanently won rank #1 against every other real queued row, including the 30 real tier-1 rows from 2026-08-04.

4. `dispatch_one()`/`run_tick()` (lines 1207-1387) only ever evaluate the single top-ranked row per call, and `run_tick()`'s loop breaks the instant that row's action isn't `"dispatched"`. Confirmed live: `dispatch_core.py`'s `has_resource_headroom()` load-average veto (`cpu_count()*0.80=6.4` on this real 8-core box) was chronically tripped (`load1=18.25` observed live), so the poison-pill row was frequently `"deferred"` — and every real tick it was, nothing else in the entire queue was even attempted (`resource_governor_tick.log` real tail: repeated `{"action": "deferred", ..., "umr_id": "UMR-20260730-181923-f2cd"}`).

## Fix

- **`directive_engine.py`**: replace the ephemeral in-memory retry flag with a real, durable check against the row's own persisted `reason` column (already set by `submit()` to `"resubmitted (reused umr_id, prior status was ...)"` on exactly the one real retry this code intends). Durable across process restarts and `DIRECTIVE.yaml` reloads. Also makes `note_needs_review()`'s `PENDING_OWNER_REVIEW.md` append idempotent (this project already hit an unbounded-repeat-log incident once — see `resource_governor_tick_loop.sh`'s own header comment — guarded here before it could recur for this file). Also makes the previously-hardcoded path constants env-overridable (same convention as `superboss-register.py`'s own `SUPERBOSS_REGISTER_DB`) — needed for real, isolated tests; production defaults unchanged.

- **`resource_governor.py`**: new `flag_stale_queued_tasks()`, wired into `run_tick()` (called by `--tick`, invoked every 30s by the always-on `veridian-governor-tick.service` — **not** part of the 19-unit closed cron-timer set per `~/.config/systemd/user/README.md`, so no new systemd unit is added). Any `status='queued'` row older than `VERIDIAN_GOVERNOR_MAX_QUEUED_AGE_S` (default 4h — chosen well above every legitimate transient concurrency/headroom delay actually observed in this investigation's own log samples, well below the multi-day silence found) gets exactly one real, idempotent `pm_decisions_pending` row opened via `insert_pm_decision_pending()` — never a raw `UPDATE`/`DELETE` against `umr_tasks`, never auto-resolved by this function. Zero AI judgment in the detection itself.

## Tests
- `tests/test_directive_engine_retry_gate.py` (5 tests)
- `tests/test_flag_stale_queued_tasks.py` (6 tests)
- Both use real, isolated, temp-file SQLite databases — never the live production database (verified via SHA-256 identical before/after).
- Full existing suite: 193 passed, no regressions.

## Real before/after evidence
- Before this investigation started: 30 tier-1 queued rows.
- During investigation (organic real production activity from the still-unpatched live `directive_engine.py`/`resource_governor.py` services, confirmed via `ts_submitted`/`ts_dispatched` timestamps, not caused by this PR's changes): count moved to 29, and `PHASE-3-BUILD-CALC` itself transitioned to `rejected_duplicate` (terminal) — directly consistent with the diagnosed mechanism.
- A dry run of the new `flag_stale_queued_tasks()` against production (later cleaned up/reverted via canonical `resolve_pm_decision_pending()`, see child UMR for full detail) confirmed 19 further real stale tier-1 rows correctly identified with accurate real age/evidence.

Real full trace, line citations, and per-row evidence recorded in child UMR (minted via `upsert_umr_task()`, `metadata.parent_umr=UMR-20260806-090229-f2a7`).

  consistent with the real `category_name` for each index in it.
- **Blocked vs pending is genuinely indistinguishable in the real schema**:
  `gtm_certification_categories.passed` is INTEGER with exactly 3 real
  values (1/0/NULL) -- confirmed no column anywhere distinguishes a
  genuinely-blocked row from a merely-pending one. Per the UMR's own

- **certified boolean** = the existing real `deterministic_gate.gate_result
  == "pass"` -- not a new field invented for this rule.
- **Overall percent is computed once**, shared by Section 2's render and
  Section 4, so the two numbers can never diverge in a single report (now

## Real Owner directive UMR-20260806-084306-f599, Step 6 (parent UMR-20260806-071025-1d28)

Steps 1-5 (integrity checks, fresh verified backup, ~21.5GB manual cleanup, node_modules
reclaim) were already done directly by the coordinator this cycle. This PR is Step 6:
the retention policy + root-cause fix so the bloat cannot silently reaccumulate again
(it already had, twice, by the time this PR was opened -- 20 more redundant copies had
accumulated in the hours between the coordinator's manual cleanup and this fix).

### What's added

1. **`prune_memory_backups.py`** -- keeps at most the 3 most recent backups that pass a
   real, freshly-run `PRAGMA integrity_check` (never trusted from a previous run),
   scanning both `.../memory/` root (the legacy ad-hoc-copy location) and
   `.../memory/backups/` (the canonical location) as **one combined keep-3 budget**.
   Groups a backup's `-wal`/`-shm` companions with it for deletion. **Hard safety gate**:
   refuses to delete anything at all -- exits non-zero, real error, zero filesystem
   writes -- unless the LIVE database itself first passes its own real
   `PRAGMA integrity_check`.
   - `--dry-run` prints the exact real plan without deleting anything.
   - `--keep` / `--scan-dir` / `--live-db` overrides for testability.
   - 15 new real tests (`tests/test_prune_memory_backups.py`), all building real sqlite
     files via `sqlite3` DDL/`.backup()` and driving the real functions/CLI -- no mocking
     of `sqlite3` or the filesystem.

2. **Root-cause fix**: `migrate_2026-07-31_dedup_constraints.py`'s own `_backup_db()`
   wrote its pre-migration snapshot as a sibling of `DB_PATH` (directly into
   `.../ai-os/memory/`) -- exactly the pattern that produced the
   `.pre-dedup-constraint-backup-*` files found during cleanup. Now writes into
   `DB_PATH`'s own `backups/` subdirectory, so the new retention policy actually
   governs it.

3. **Systemd timer** -- `~/.config/systemd/user/veridian-cron-prune-memory-backups.{service,timer}`,
   daily at 04:47 UTC (jittered, `RandomizedDelaySec=600`), gated by the same
   `resource-governor-EMERGENCY_STOP` sentinel every other unit uses. This is unit #19,
   an explicit-Owner-authorized exception to the systemd README's closed-set-of-18 rule
   (README updated in the same change) -- this directive is itself the required explicit
   Owner decision for a genuinely new cadence/purpose (doesn't fit the nearest analog,
   `credit-ledger-prune`, which prunes an unrelated financial ledger for an unrelated
   reason).

### Root-cause search -- what I found and didn't find

Searched every `.py`/`.sh` under `/opt/veridian/scripts` for `shutil.copy`/`.backup(`/
`open(...,"wb")`/subprocess `cp` near `superboss-register.sqlite`, `SUPERBOSS_REGISTER_DB`,
and `MEMORY_DIR`-style variables (not just literal path matches, since the directive
warned the path is likely variable/f-string constructed). Found exactly **one** other
live script with this pattern: `migrate_2026-07-31_dedup_constraints.py`, fixed above.

`health-check-15min.py` and `gtm_check_backup_recovery_testing.py` already write/read
only `/opt/veridian/backups/sqlite-daily/` -- a different, already-correct location
(PR #144, confirmed not touched here).

**Said plainly**: the other backup-naming conventions found in the live directory
(`bak-ACCIDENTAL-*`, `pre-stageN-*`, `pre-utm-*`, `rebuild-2026-07-23*`,
`vacuum-2026-07-23-phase9`, `pre-repair-phase1-*`) do **not** correspond to any current
live script under `/opt/veridian/scripts` -- they were one-off manual/session operations,
not reusable scripts, so there is no live root-cause script left to fix for those.
`prune_memory_backups.py`'s retention policy is what actually closes that gap going
forward (it deletes them regardless of which naming convention produced them).

Search command used:
```
grep -rln "shutil\.copy\|\.backup(\|BACKUP_DIR\|backup_dir\|BACKUP_PATH\|superboss-register\.sqlite" \
  --include="*.py" --include="*.sh" . | grep -v '\.bak\|/archive/\|superseded'
```
plus targeted greps for each specific backup-suffix string found in the live directory
listing, and a broad `grep -rl "backup"` cross-referenced against every file that also
mentions `.sqlite`, to catch variable-constructed paths.

**Hard exclusion honored**: `/opt/veridian/scripts/dispatch-owner-task.sh` was checked
(currently has zero `superboss-register.sqlite` references) and **not modified** --
it's owned this cycle by UMR-20260806-085144-9c63.

**Dry-run** (`python3 prune_memory_backups.py --dry-run`, run before any real deletion):
kept the 3 most recent verified backups, planned to delete 13 groups totaling
1,611,927,552 bytes (~1.50 GiB) -- full JSON plan in the PR discussion / task evidence.

**Real run** (`python3 prune_memory_backups.py`, no flags) executed against the live
`/opt/veridian/ai-os/memory` directly, using the script itself (not manual `rm`) --

`python3 -m pytest tests/ -q` (full suite, this branch): **159 passed**.

Prevention side only. Reconciliation of already-stale `umr_tasks` rows is **out of scope here** -- that's PR #147 (`reconcile_owner_dispatch_status.py`, `UMR-20260806-082646-3aba`), untouched by this PR.

`dispatch-owner-task.sh` mints a real UMR via `resource_governor.py --submit`, logs the instruction/work-item pair via `superboss-register.py`, then relays the same message into the live interactive tmux session -- but never wrote `ts_dispatched`, `status`, or a terminal outcome back onto the `umr_tasks` row it just created. Confirmed this cycle against `UMR-20260806-084306-f599` / `UMR-20260806-084542-3c43`: both did real, verified work but still read `status='queued'`, `ts_dispatched=NULL`. This is why `PERCENT_COMPLETE_24H_OWNER_UMR_SET` stays low and why reconciliation sweeps keep having to guess.

## What it does

- **`superboss-register.py`**: two new CLI subcommands over the existing real `update_umr_task()`, following the `insert-pm-decision-pending`/`resolve-pm-decision-pending` wrapper convention exactly (thin CLI entry point, `_write_lock()`, prints real JSON, never a raw SQL `UPDATE`):
  - `mark-umr-dispatched --umr-id UMR-... [--unit-name NAME]` -- writes real `ts_dispatched` + `status='dispatched'`.
  - `mark-umr-terminal --umr-id UMR-... --status {completed,failed,killed} [--reason TEXT]` -- writes real `ts_completed` + a real terminal status. Two callers: `dispatch-owner-task.sh`'s relay-failure branch (`--status failed`), and any worker/interactive session recording genuine completion once real work finishes.

- **`dispatch-owner-task.sh`**: calls `mark-umr-dispatched` immediately after the real tmux relay succeeds; calls `mark-umr-terminal --status failed` (with a real reason) on the relay-not-found branch, so a row is never silently left at `queued`. Adds `DISPATCH_TMUX_SESSION` (default: `claude`, unchanged default behavior) purely as a testability seam -- lets a caller point the relay at a disposable session instead of the real live one. Exact command forms documented in the script's own header comment.

- **`tests/test_dispatch_owner_task_status_write.py`** (9 new tests): the two CLI subcommands against a real, isolated, temp-file scratch DB (never production); `dispatch-owner-task.sh`'s own relay-succeeds / relay-fails / `--no-relay` branching exercised end-to-end with a deterministic fake-`tmux` shim on `PATH` (no real tmux server dependency in CI, no risk to any real live session).

## Verification

- Real end-to-end run against an isolated scratch DB + a disposable tmux session named `claude-relay-test-throwaway` (never production, never the real live `claude` session -- independently confirmed untouched via `tmux capture-pane` immediately before and after):

  - Simulated real completion via `mark-umr-terminal --status completed` on the dispatched row: `status='completed'`, `ts_completed` populated, `ts_dispatched` preserved unchanged from the earlier write.

## Scope / collision notes

- Never touches any pre-existing `umr_tasks` row -- only rows this script itself mints going forward. No overlap with PR #147's reconciliation logic or write path.
- Verified fresh (not just relied on an earlier claim) via `systemctl --user list-units 'veridian-worker@*' --state=running`: two units were running at development time (`...close-all-real-owner-dispatched-umrs-fro`, `...merge-pr-959-compliance-tracker...`); confirmed via `systemctl --user show ... -p ExecStart` that both invoke `worker-entrypoint.sh` against unrelated task IDs, not this file or its tmux/DB write path -- not a real collision for this change.

Root-cause fix, UMR-20260806-082352-7b1b (child of Owner directive UMR-20260806-081403-ebd3).

## Root cause

`backfill_null_heartbeats()`'s systemd-dispatched-rows branch (`resource_governor.py`, ~line 1720-1751 before this PR) unconditionally marked a NULL-heartbeat, `systemctl --user is-active`-confirmed-inactive row `status='failed'`, without ever reading the task's own real `task.yaml` under `/opt/veridian/ai-os/tasks/<task_id>/` first.

Live-confirmed this cycle by manual inspection of 9 real rows:
- 6 were genuinely "blocked with real forward progress" (real commits/PRs, blocked only by credit-accountant/branch-protection/tier2-signoff gates) and mislabeled `failed`.
- 1 was genuinely `completed` (PR #55 merged) and mislabeled `failed`.
- 2 were correctly `failed` after independent verification — their claimed task.yaml progress did not hold up (e.g. one branch's tip commit predated its own task's start time).

## Fix

Before defaulting to `failed`, the function now real-checks the task's `task.yaml` (read via `dispatch_core.task_status_sync()`, the existing canonical reader — never a second parallel glob/parse of TASKS_DIR):

1. `task.yaml` already terminal-negative (`failed`/`cancelled`/`rejected_duplicate`/`superseded`/`not_needed`) → no override, stays `failed`.
2. A referenced PR (`adopted_pr_url`, or a checkpoint note's `pull/NNN` URL) is cross-checked via a real `gh pr view --json state,mergedAt,mergeCommit,url`:
   - `MERGED` → `completed`
   - `OPEN` → `running`
   - `CLOSED` (unmerged) → `failed` (as before)
   - unverifiable (timeout/error) → `failed` (fail toward the original default)
3. No PR referenced, but `status: blocked` with a referenced `branch`: the branch's own real tip-commit date (`gh api repos/<org>/<repo>/commits/<branch>`) must postdate the task's own real `created_at` — this is the exact check that catches a stale/unrelated branch reference, the real failure mode behind 2 of the 9 live rows. If it doesn't hold up → stays `failed`.
4. No PR/commit evidence at all → original default, stays `failed`.

A task.yaml's own claims are never trusted on their own — every branch above ends in `failed` unless independently, real cross-checked evidence positively justifies `running`/`completed`.

Also checked `dispatch_core.py` per the parent directive's framing ("dispatch_core.py or resource_governor.py"): it has no `status='failed'` assignment anywhere (confirmed via a direct source scan for `failed`/`heartbeat`/`is-active` — no matches beyond two unrelated non-fatal log warnings), so no fix was needed there.

## Tests

`tests/test_backfill_null_heartbeats_task_yaml_crosscheck.py` — 11 new tests, all passing, against a real isolated scratch SQLite DB and real temp `task.yaml` files on disk; only the three real external boundary calls (`systemctl --user is-active`, `gh pr view`, `gh api .../commits/<branch>`) are mocked, via one fake `_run` dispatcher keyed on real command shape:

- merged / open / closed-unmerged referenced-PR cases
- the branch-tip-commit-predates-task-creation case (the real 2-of-9 failure mode)
- no-task.yaml and no-evidence fallback-to-`failed` cases
- unverifiable-`gh`-call fallback
- `task.yaml` already terminal-negative → no override
- dry-run (`execute=False`) never writes, even when evidence says `completed`
- active-unit-left-alone regression (unchanged behavior)

Full suite: **285 passed**. 6 pre-existing failures in the untracked `test_dispatch_tick_heartbeat.py` (stale `dispatch-tick.py` attribute names) are unrelated — that file is not touched by this branch and was already untracked/broken before this change.

## Live dry-run re-verification

See PR comment below for a dry-run (`execute=False`) re-run of the fixed logic against the current live 24h `owner_dispatch_gateway` NULL-heartbeat set.

## Real governance finding (UMR-20260806-075726-babc, child of UMR-20260806-071025-1d28)

A real governance finding this cycle: `umr_tasks` rows with `source_trigger='owner_dispatch_gateway'` commonly get stuck showing `status='running'` after the worker session backing them dies without a graceful terminal-status write. At requery time this PR was built (2026-08-06T08:12Z), 30 rows matched `source_trigger='owner_dispatch_gateway' AND status='running'` in the trailing 24h, cross-referenced against `systemctl --user list-units 'veridian-worker@*' --state=running`, which showed only 4 real running units -- confirming 26 of the 30 rows carried a false `running` label.

This promotes the scratchpad one-off classifier used for this cycle's manual cleanup (`classify_owner_dispatch_backlog.py`) into a real, tested, re-runnable production script, since this same staleness problem recurs.

## What it does

For every `status='running'` row (last 24h, `source_trigger='owner_dispatch_gateway'`), cross-checks 3 independent real signals -- never narrated:
1. real systemd unit state for the row's `unit_name` (`systemctl --user is-active`)
2. real `task.yaml` checkpoint under `/opt/veridian/ai-os/tasks/<task_id>/`
3. real GitHub PR state + `AUDIT:PASS`/`FAIL` comment freshness (matched against the PR's current head SHA)

Buckets deterministically into `REAL_RUNNING` / `STALE_LABEL_TERMINAL` / `NEEDS_AI_JUDGMENT`. Only `STALE_LABEL_TERMINAL` rows are auto-corrected: PR MERGED -> `completed`, PR CLOSED-not-merged -> `failed`, no PR ever opened -> `killed`. **A real OPEN PR is never auto-terminalized**, even one already carrying a fresh, current-head-SHA `AUDIT:PASS` -- resolving those needs a real continuation/merge action or genuine judgment, not a mechanical relabel.

That last rule exists because of a real bug caught during this script's own build: an earlier version blanket-mapped `task.yaml status='blocked'` to DB `status='failed'`, which on the real live 26-row set would have mislabeled ~18 rows that actually have a real open, often-passing PR one merge away from done -- matching this project's own established precedent (`batch3_summary_draft.txt` under UMR-20260806-071025-1d28: an inactive-systemd/blocked-task.yaml row with a real open PR was re-adopted and continued, never blanket-failed). Regression test: `test_open_pr_never_auto_terminalized_even_with_fresh_audit_pass`.

## Write path

All corrections go **only** through `superboss-register.py`'s own `update_umr_task()`, inside its own `_write_lock()`, one commit per invocation -- never a raw SQL `UPDATE`. Enforced by `test_apply_correction_writes_only_via_update_umr_task` (uses a connection stub that raises `AssertionError` if `.execute()` is ever called directly). Default mode is report-only (zero writes, and correspondingly never takes the write lock, so it never contends with a real live writer); `--apply` performs corrections; `--json PATH` writes full per-row evidence.

## Verification

- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_reconcile_owner_dispatch_status.py -q` -> 10 passed
- `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q` (full existing suite) -> 154 passed
- Ran live against the production DB in report-only mode (no writes): confirms the real 4 REAL_RUNNING / ~26 STALE_LABEL_TERMINAL+NEEDS_AI_JUDGMENT split described above (exact counts drift row-to-row since the live dispatch queue keeps submitting new rows every few seconds).

## Known live collision, not raced

At build time, `veridian-worker@task-20260806-075804-close-all-real-owner-dispatched-umrs-fro.service` (owning UMR-20260806-071025-1d28, this PR's own parent UMR) was independently, genuinely running the broader 95-row owner-dispatch backlog closure with its own equivalent playbook. Per this project's standing "never race a duplicate-dispatch collision" rule, `--apply` was deliberately not run against the live DB from this PR's own build session; see the linked child UMR's evidence for the collision check and hold decision. This script is meant to be the durable, reusable tool for that live task (and every future recurrence of this same staleness problem) to reuse going forward, not a one-time competing sweep.

`capability_registry` was checked and is scoped to product/business-domain capabilities (gratuity calculator, GST engine, document OCR, etc.) -- not the right registration surface for this internal ops script, so it is not registered there.

3. **Fixed exclude list added**: `COLLISION_FILE_OVERLAP_EXCLUDE_FILES` = `PROGRESS.md`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `bun.lock`, `yarn.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `ai-os/boss/ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml`, `ai-os/CONSTITUTION.yaml`, `src/lib/db/schema.ts`, `tsconfig.json`.
4. **Hard output cap regardless of 1-3**: primary ranked before secondary (`_rank_collision_candidates`), top 50 of >200 candidates shown with an honest summary count (`_cap_collision_candidates`).

## Summary

Owner standing mandate (task-20260806-034817, cites UMR-20260805-185000-e94f):
"thinking is by the Project Manager, execution is by AI agents, AI agents do not
think for themselves." Builds the full deposit -> PM-decide -> AI-completion
lifecycle for real novel findings outside already-approved scope into
`superboss-register.py` (the one canonical read/write script) and its database,
and wires the pending-proposal list into `generate_pm_report_v3.py`.

This gate is **not retroactive** to already-authorized broad-category work in
flight (e.g. the GTM script build) -- nothing existing was changed to force this
gate onto it; it's purely additive and opt-in for future novel findings.

## Extend-vs-new-table decision

Extended `pm_decisions_pending` rather than building a second parallel table.
Full reasoning in `PROGRESS.md`, short version: 7 of 8 needed fields already
existed on the table (title/detail/related_umr/status/closed_ts/closed_by/
closed_note map directly onto issue/proposal/child_umr/decision/PM-name/PM-note);
only the completion-evidence phase needed new columns. One discriminator column,
`decision_type` (the SPEC's own suggested example), keeps the two real row shapes
from ever crossing.

## Changes

**`superboss-register.py`**
- `_migrate_pm_decisions_pending_owner_proposal_columns()` -- additive migration:
  `decision_type` (NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pm_decision'), `completed_ts`,
  `artifact_path`, `commit_sha`, `evidence`
- `insert_owner_proposal(conn, issue, proposal, *, child_umr=None)` -- AI deposits
  a proposal; mints a real child UMR via the existing `_new_id("UMR")` convention
- `decide_owner_proposal(conn, decision_id, *, decision, closed_by, closed_note=None)`
  -- PM approves/redirects/holds, citing the child UMR
- `record_owner_proposal_completion(conn, decision_id, *, artifact_path, commit_sha, evidence)`
  -- AI records real completion evidence back onto the same row, idempotent
- `resolve_pm_decision_pending()` gained optional `require_decision_type=None`
  (100% backward compatible) so `decide_owner_proposal()` reuses it, zero duplication
- 3 new CLI subcommands: `insert-owner-proposal`, `decide-owner-proposal`,
  `record-owner-proposal-completion`

**`generate_pm_report_v3.py`**
- New **Section 8: AI PROPOSALS AWAITING PM DECISION** -- same read-only pattern
  Section 7 already uses for `pm_decisions_pending`
- `get_pm_decisions_pending()` now excludes `owner_proposal` rows; both new/old
  queries degrade gracefully (no crash, no missing-column error) against a DB that
  predates this migration

**Tests** -- 171 passing, zero regressions:
- `tests/test_pm_decisions_pending.py`: +9 tests (deposit, explicit child UMR,
  full round trip, invalid-decision rejection, cross-type refusal,
  completion-requires-approved, completion idempotency, Section 7/8 exclusivity),
  updated live-schema column pin
- `test_generate_pm_report_v3.py`: Section 8 fixture + assertions, dedicated
  backward-compatibility test against a pre-migration schema

## Real sample output -- proposal round trip end to end

Run against a genuine isolated scratch DB (never production), through the real
CLI entry points:

```
=== 1) AI deposits a real child-UMR proposal ===
{
  "id": 1,
  "child_umr": "UMR-20260806-035851-f711"
}

=== 2) PM approves the proposal, citing its child UMR ===
{
  "id": 1,
  "decision": "approved",
  "decided": true
}

=== 3) AI records real completion evidence back onto the same row ===
{
  "id": 1,
  "recorded": true
}

=== Final row state ===
{
  "id": 1,
  "title": "real issue: task-gateway.py's dispatch validator has no check for duplicate concurrent dispatch of the same task_identity within a 5s window",
  "detail": "AI proposes: add a real short-TTL in-memory/DB lock keyed on task_identity to task-gateway.py's cmd_start(), rejecting a second dispatch of the same identity within the window instead of racing",
  "related_umr": "UMR-20260806-035851-f711",
  "status": "completed",
  "closed_by": "pm-agent",
  "closed_note": "approved -- proceed under UMR-20260806-035851-f711",
  "decision_type": "owner_proposal",
  "artifact_path": "task-gateway.py",
  "commit_sha": "0000000000000000000000000000000000dead",
  "evidence": "demo evidence only -- real PR/commit to follow for UMR-20260806-035851-f711"
}

=== 4) generate_pm_report_v3.py Section 8 rendering a still-open proposal ===
[

    "id": 2,
    "issue": "real issue: demo of an OPEN proposal still awaiting PM decision",
    "proposal": "AI proposes: nothing yet, this one is deliberately left open for the demo",
    "child_umr": "UMR-20260806-035851-46a6",

## Root cause (already investigated, not re-litigated here)

No active mechanism produces backups for `/opt/veridian/ai-os/memory/superboss-register.sqlite` anywhere on this box -- confirmed via `systemctl --user list-timers` (nothing matches), `crontab -l` (empty), and a repo-wide grep. `health-check-15min.py`'s existing `check_db_integrity_and_backup()` raw-copies a backup, but only once the **entire** live database passes a full-database `PRAGMA integrity_check` first -- so while even one table stays corrupted, no backup is ever written at all, healthy tables included. Category 19 is currently `fail`: superboss-register.sqlite's last real backup is from 2026-08-03, now 64.3h+ old (48h bar).

## What this PR adds

1. **`sqlite_daily_backup.py`** -- a real, idempotent backup generator that:
   - Uses SQLite's own online backup API (`sqlite3.Connection.backup()`) -- never a raw file copy against a live WAL-mode database under concurrent writers.
   - Independently runs `PRAGMA integrity_check` against the **resulting backup file itself** (not the source, not just "non-empty") before considering the backup successful.
   - Fails loudly (non-zero exit, clear stderr) and quarantines the bad artifact under a name `gtm_check_backup_recovery_testing.py`'s `<db>.<YYYYMMDD>.bak` glob will never match, if the backup comes out corrupt or zero-byte -- never a silent false success. This is the exact failure mode the task exists to prevent recurring.
   - Idempotent: a same-day backup that already exists and re-verifies ok is a clean no-op skip; one that no longer verifies is quarantined and redone.

2. **`tests/test_sqlite_daily_backup.py`** -- 8 real tests, all against small SYNTHETIC sqlite fixtures built in a tempdir, **never against the real live database**:
   - Happy path (real online backup + integrity verify against a healthy synthetic db).
   - **The critical negative test**: a deliberately-corrupted synthetic source database (real structural corruption -- verified empirically to trip `PRAGMA integrity_check` with "database disk image is malformed", not assumed/fabricated) must cause `BackupError` and must never leave a file at the real dated backup path that passes integrity_check.
   - A backup file corrupted *after* being written (simulating post-write disk damage) is detected, quarantined, and a fresh one is correctly produced on re-run.
   - Idempotent skip-on-verified, `--force` override, missing-source handling, zero-byte-result quarantine, and an end-to-end CLI `main()` test proving a mixed healthy+corrupt batch exits non-zero while still completing the healthy one.
   - **All 8 pass locally** (see test results below).

3. **`systemd/veridian-cron-sqlite-daily-backup.service` + `.timer`** -- follows the existing `veridian-cron-credit-ledger-prune.service`/`.timer` pattern exactly (same `ConditionPathExists` load-shed gate, `run-logged.sh` wrapper, jittered `OnCalendar`, `RandomizedDelaySec`). Verified with `systemd-analyze --user verify` (clean, exit 0).

## NOT enabled / NOT started -- disclosed explicitly

These unit files are committed to this repo's `systemd/` directory only. They have **deliberately not been copied into `~/.config/systemd/user/`, not enabled, and not started** on the real box. Two independent gates, both documented in each unit file's own header comment, still block real activation:

1. **Closed-set-of-18 rule** (`~/.config/systemd/user/README.md`): the 18 existing `veridian-cron-*` pairs are a closed set; a genuinely new unit "requires an explicit Owner decision to add unit #19 -- never a default/automatic action by any script, worker, or session." The PM authorization for this task (UMR-20260805-171657-01de) covers building/testing the script and timer construction -- it is a PM decision, not the separate Owner-level decision the closed-set rule itself calls for. Flagging this distinction explicitly rather than quietly treating "build the timer" as also authorizing "install it as unit #19."
2. **file_inventory corruption precondition (Hard Rule 8)**: `superboss-register.sqlite` has one real, confirmed-corrupted table (`file_inventory` -- fails `PRAGMA integrity_check` and even `DROP TABLE`), held for a real Owner recovery decision. A full-file online backup of that specific live database will currently fail. Independently confirmed before writing any code (direct sqlite query against `umr_tasks`/`gtm_certification_categories`, no resolution UMR found under the parent, category 19 still failing on staleness) that this precondition remains unresolved as of this PR.

Both gates must clear -- a real Owner decision on #1, and a real `PRAGMA integrity_check` confirming "ok" against the live database on #2 -- before this timer is ever installed/enabled against the real live database.

## Explicit confirmation

At no point during this task did any command read from, write to, or run any check (including `PRAGMA integrity_check`) against the real live `file_inventory` table, or attempt a real full-database backup or full-database `PRAGMA integrity_check` against the real live `superboss-register.sqlite`. All script development and all 8 tests ran exclusively against synthetic sqlite fixtures created in a tempdir for this task. The only real-database interaction this task performed was read-only `SELECT` queries against the `umr_tasks` and `gtm_certification_categories` tables (via `sqlite3 -readonly`) to fetch the original task instructions and independently verify the corruption-precondition's current state -- neither of which touches `file_inventory` or runs any integrity/backup operation.

Once merged and once BOTH gates above have independently cleared, the followup step (re-running `gtm_check_backup_recovery_testing.py` and updating category 19 honestly) is explicitly deferred, not attempted in this PR.

## Summary

Owner directive (UMR-20260805-034917-33a9, OD-20260805-001) asked for a real, separate GitHub App or service-account identity to independently review compliance-tracker PRs, distinct from the sole account (`FChecklist`) that authors them, plus an automated check that reviewer and author are never the same account.

## What I found before changing anything

Checked the dispatch's claims against the live GitHub API rather than taking them at face value:

| Claim | Live fact |
|---|---|
| Branch protection requires 1 approving review | `required_approving_review_count` is currently **0** |
| ~12 PRs stuck | **100+** open PRs |

The core problem is still real: `FChecklist` is the sole collaborator on compliance-tracker, and every credential in this environment (`gh auth`, `$GITHUB_PAT`, `$GITHUB_PAT_ZAI_KIMI`) independently resolves to that same account via `GET /user`. No genuinely independent identity exists anywhere here.

## What I did NOT do, and why

- Did **not** fabricate a "second identity" by relabeling the existing FChecklist credential — that's explicitly the anti-pattern the directive warns against, and GitHub would still record the same account as approver.
- Did **not** attempt scripted GitHub account creation — against ToS, and there's no email inbox in this environment to complete verification anyway.
- Did **not** flip `required_approving_review_count` to 1 on compliance-tracker — doing that *before* a real second identity is installed as a collaborator would immediately block 100% of future PRs (GitHub already refuses self-approval), which is a regression against OD-20260805-001's actual goal of unblocking queued work.

Creating a genuinely independent identity (new personal account, or the correct mechanism — a GitHub App with its own `[bot]` actor) requires an interactive GitHub web-UI step by a human with email/browser access. That isn't achievable from this environment's headless API/CLI tools, so it's the one remaining step a human needs to do — full instructions in the new doc below.

## What this PR delivers

- `superboss-register.py`: `refuse_review_if_reviewer_is_author()` / `apply_review_independence_verdict()` — the automated reviewer-≠-author check, mirroring the existing `refuse_certification_if_merged_without_required_checks()` pure-function pattern. Not yet wired into a live merge gate (nothing to check against until the real identity exists) but ready to call the moment it is.
- `tests/test_ocid_master_standard_phase1.py`: 5 new passing tests for the above.
- `OCID_070_SECOND_REVIEWER_IDENTITY_PROVISIONING_FINDING_2026-08-05.md`: full write-up of the premise check and the concrete remaining steps for whoever provisions the real identity.
- `PROGRESS.md` updated.

## Review note

Per the directive: this specific PR is requested to go through the real Owner account for review, one time, since the new reviewer identity doesn't exist yet to review its own creation. Opening as a normal PR for that review rather than self-merging.

Citing **UMR-20260804-170055-a069** (canonical OCID-068 UMR) and **UMR-20260805-032326-becc** (real OCID canonical roster build).

## What this PR does

**1. Standardizes the schema (`superboss-register.py`)**
- `EVIDENCE_JSON_REQUIRED_KEYS` + `validate_evidence_json_schema()`: every required key must be *present* (an honest `null` is valid for every key except `evidence_summary`); `evidence_summary` must be a real non-empty sentence. Extra keys (e.g. preserved legacy free-text evidence) are always allowed — nothing is forced out.
- `_status_claims_verified_or_completed()`: a real, deterministic, whole-word/non-negated detector for whether a row's free-text `status` genuinely claims completion. Independently verified against all 69 live rows — 11 real matches, and it correctly excludes two real false-positive traps already present in the data (`"running, never completed"`, `"...ts_completed=null"` / `"NOT_VERIFIED"`).
- `refuse_ocid_registry_completion_if_evidence_incomplete()`: a pure, zero-I/O, second independent refusal gate, placed alongside — never replacing — `refuse_certification_if_merged_without_required_checks()` from PR #54.
- Wired directly into `upsert_ocid_canonical_registry()`: when a row's status genuinely claims completed/verified and its `evidence_json` doesn't satisfy the schema, the write is refused (`OcidEvidenceSchemaRefused` raised, nothing written) and a real, permanent `evidence_schema_refused` audit event is recorded. Rows not claiming completion are completely unaffected — no behavior change for them.
- `tests/test_evidence_json_schema_gate.py` — 11 new tests. Updated 3 already-merged tests whose seed fixtures used `status="completed"` with legacy-shape evidence to use schema-complete evidence (same original assertions/intent preserved).

**2. Backfills the 69 real existing rows (`backfill_evidence_json_schema.py`)**
- Rewrites every row's `evidence_json` to the new shape, preserving each row's own pre-existing `evidence_json` verbatim under a new `legacy_evidence` key — no real information is discarded.
- Real provenance note: mid-task, a separate concurrent real run of `backfill_ocid_registry_phase2_columns.py` (OCID-068 Phase 2, already-merged PR #57) had just actually populated the dedicated `commit_sha`/`file_name`/`file_path`/`merge_status`/`evidence_summary` columns against this same live production DB via real `gh pr view` calls. Rather than duplicate that same recovery a second time, this script reads those already-real columns directly. Zero duplicate implementation.
- Applied against the live DB after a dry-run review and a pre-write backup. Verified after: all 69 rows are schema-compliant; the 11 rows whose status genuinely claims completed/verified pass the enforced gate.

## Tests

`python3 -m pytest tests/ -q` → **113 passed**.

## Scope note

Deliberately narrow, per this codebase's own established discipline (small, independently-reviewed increments): this PR only standardizes `evidence_json`'s shape and enforces it at the write path used by the existing OCID canonical-registry tooling. It does not change `resolve_ocid_canonical()`'s own return shape (still exercised/tested independently elsewhere) or the OCID-068 Phase 2 dedicated-column backfill mechanism itself (PR #57) — it reuses that mechanism's already-real output.

Deliberately narrow, following this repo's own established precedent (OCID-068's seven guardrail rules were each their own separate, independently-reviewed PR: #26, #29, #30, #32, #33, #34, #35) rather than one giant unreviewable PR. 1. **`resolve_ocid_canonical()`** -- locks down one canonical OCID->UMR resolution methodology (a: `umr_tasks.task_identity` substring match across casings -> b: full-table dump+grep, never (a) alone -> c: `gh pr list --search` across all 3 repos -> d: `git log --grep` cross-check -> e: PR-body UMR-ID extraction -> f: `MASTER-TRACKER`/`ACTIVE-CLAIMS` last resort). 2. **`reconcile_umr_status_against_pr()`** -- cross-checks `umr_tasks.status`/`ts_completed` against real PR-merge evidence, returns a proposed correction without silently auto-applying it (caller applies via existing `update_umr_task()`, same pattern as `UMR-20260805-024319-b1e6`'s earlier correction). 3. **`refuse_certification_if_merged_without_required_checks()`** -- pure, independent, redundant certification-refusal logic. A real search (`git log --grep`, `grep -ril`) across fresh clones of compliance-tracker, veridian-scripts, and projexa found no prior "OCID Master Standard version 5.1" document anywhere. This PR does not claim one exists.

## Summary
Real root-cause investigation and fix (`UMR-20260804-213847-4b56`, citing `UMR-20260804-180711-7f96`) of the two real automated-duplicate-worker incidents this session observed and stopped mid-flight.

## Real root cause, confirmed directly (not guessed)
Queried the real live `umr_tasks` table for the exact `ts_submitted`/`ts_dispatched` timestamps of the first incident's 5 re-fired tasks:

| UMR | ts_submitted | ts_dispatched | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| UMR-20260804-194151-4a59 | 19:41:51 | 20:55:35 | 74 min |
| UMR-20260804-194323-0bc5 | 19:43:23 | 20:55:39 | 72 min |
| UMR-20260804-194343-e28e | 19:43:43 | 20:55:44 | 72 min |
| UMR-20260804-194355-be9c | 19:43:55 | 20:55:48 | 72 min |
| UMR-20260804-194407-6148 | 19:44:07 | 20:55:52 | 72 min |

All 5 are the **same original row** (same `task_identity`, same `umr_id`), never re-inserted -- not a retry loop, not a duplicate cron trigger, not a notification delivered more than once.

**Real cause**: `dispatch-owner-task.sh`'s own real, by-design dual dispatch relays every real Owner/PM instruction into **both** the live interactive tmux session **and** a real, governed `veridian_task_create` task in the same `umr_tasks` queue, in the same call (see that script's own header comment -- deliberate, for laptop-independence: the queued twin still runs even if the interactive session goes away). The real, previously-missing piece: nothing ever told the queued twin the interactive channel already finished the same real work. Real anti-starvation aging (`effective_priority()`) plus real concurrency backpressure (this session's own heavy interactive slot usage occupying real worker/supervisor slots for extended stretches) left these tasks queued 72-74 real minutes -- by which time the same UMRs' work had already been completed and merged via the interactive channel.

## The real fix
Inside the existing canonical `dispatch_one()` chokepoint (`resource_governor.py`), not a new parallel system: before spawning a queued `veridian_task_create` task, check whether its own title names a real OCID (regex extraction, normalized to the real `OCID-NNN` zero-padded format `ocid_artifact_links` already uses) that already has real evidence in `ocid_artifact_links` created **after** this row's own `ts_submitted`. If so, that is real, direct proof the same OCID's work was independently completed while this task waited -- skip the redundant spawn (`status=rejected_duplicate`, `action=superseded_by_ocid_evidence`, a new Rule 2 outcome mapped to `"rejected"`) instead of duplicating already-finished real work, and log the real supersession via `_append_attention()` for PM/Owner visibility (never silently dropped).

Deliberately narrow and evidence-based, never heuristic: only fires for `veridian_task_create` rows (`systemctl_action`/resume rows are untouched, same real scope as the pre-existing duplicate-PR guard), only on a real regex-extracted OCID number, only when real **newer** evidence exists (older evidence, or no evidence, changes nothing -- genuinely new work is never blocked).

## Tests
5 new real tests, `tests/test_ocid_evidence_supersession.py`, against a real isolated scratch SQLite DB (never the live production database), including a **direct reproduction of the exact observed incident shape** (OCID-068, the real OCID from the first re-fire):
- the real incident is correctly superseded
- a queued task with an OCID but no newer evidence still spawns normally (never blocks new work)
- evidence that predates submission does not supersede
- a title with no OCID never matches
- `systemctl_action` rows are never checked

On completion, return the real evidence, the real files modified, the real database changes, the UMR, the OCID, the PR, the commit, the real test results, any open items, any blockers, and the real next action, no assumptions, no narration, no estimates."

## What changed
`validate_completion_evidence()` -- a pure-function structural check extending the existing "completed can never be self-reported directly" state-machine guard already in `veridian-task.py`'s `cmd_checkpoint()` (which already refuses `--status completed` unless a real `pending_review` checkpoint exists in the task's own history). That existing guard checks the **state sequence** is real; this is the complement Rule 7 names: checks the **specific evidence fields** are genuinely present, never a narrated placeholder.

New optional `--evidence-json` flag on `checkpoint`, using the exact same real, already-reviewed pre-lock-validation pattern OCID-063's own `--handoff-envelope` established: validated and rejected **before** the task lock is taken/anything is loaded or saved, so a malformed evidence file never partially writes a checkpoint. Omitting it entirely behaves exactly as before this change. Only enforced when `--status completed` is also used.

**Required fields** (`pr_url`, `commit_sha`, `test_results`, `umr_id`, `next_action`): rejected if missing **or** a narration placeholder (empty string, or one of a real generic-non-answer set -- `N/A`, `none`, `TBD`, `unknown`, etc., case-insensitive) -- the exact "declare complete from narration alone" pattern Rule 7 forbids. `pr_url`/`commit_sha`/`umr_id` are further checked against their real, known formats (a real GitHub PR URL, a real hex commit SHA, a real `UMR-<date>-<time>-<hex>` id) -- a mechanical format check that catches an obviously-fabricated value (not proof the PR is actually merged -- this function does no I/O, by deliberate design, same as `validate_handoff_envelope()`).

`open_items`/`blockers` are required **list** fields (an empty list is a real, valid "genuinely nothing open" state, not itself an error -- but a narrated string like `"no blockers"` standing in for the list is rejected). `db_changes` is intentionally optional (many real completions genuinely touch no database at all -- Rules 2/3/5/6's own PRs included plenty of code-only changes), but if present is held to the same narration-placeholder standard, with `"none"`/`"no schema or data changes"` explicitly exempted as honest claims of absence rather than vague non-answers.

`test_ocid063_handoff_envelope.py` builds raw `argparse.Namespace` objects bypassing the real CLI parser, so it lacked the new `evidence_json` attribute entirely -- a real `AttributeError`. ## Summary
Fifth real installment of the OCID-068 seven-rule guardrails addendum (Rule 5 of 7, following Rules 1-4/PRs #26, #29, #30, #31). Per `UMR-20260804-205741-cf3f` (direction to continue Rules 4-7, no pause). Checked for active/duplicate work first -- no other branch/PR addresses this scope. Note: 5 real automated duplicate workers (an exact re-fire of the entire earlier 5-way expedite batch, including one targeting this exact addendum) were found running mid-session and stopped/checkpointed with pointers to the already-real work, before this PR was opened.

**Rule 5** (verbatim, from `UMR-20260804-180711-7f96`): "real stall detection, a task is stale only if it has no heartbeat, no checkpoint, no log entry, no CPU activity, and no file change for the configured threshold, visual tmux pane text alone shall never be used by itself to declare a stall, stall detection requires this real combined evidence."

## The real, previously uncovered gap
The pre-existing `find_stuck_tasks()` only covers `status=='blocked'` tasks -- those have no running unit at all, by construction (`worker-entrypoint.sh` disables the unit before writing `blocked`). A task whose systemd unit still reports `ActiveState=active` (so it's `in_progress`, not `blocked`) but is silently hung was never checked by anything -- exactly the "real false stall concern" Rule 5's own text references: naive tmux-pane-text-only detection could wrongly call a legitimately-still-computing task stalled.

## What changed
`find_stalled_running_tasks()` -- a real, combined-evidence stall detector for `status=='in_progress'` tasks. A task is flagged **only** when **all five** real signals independently confirm no activity within `threshold_minutes`:
- no checkpoint update (`last_checkpoint_at`)
- no heartbeat update (real `umr_tasks.last_heartbeat`, looked up by `task_identity` via `resource_governor`'s own `_safe_superboss_register()` helper)
- no fresh log/file activity (real mtime walk of the task's own workspace directory -- covers both "log entry" and "file change" as one real filesystem question)
- no real CPU-tick movement (`_read_proc_cpu_ticks()`, a real `/proc/<pid>/stat` `utime+stime` read via the unit's real systemd `MainPID`, with a cross-tick delta persisted to a new `TASK_CPU_STATE.json` -- same pattern `resource_governor.sample_metrics()` already establishes for host-wide metrics)

Any signal that cannot be determined (DB unavailable, no `MainPID`, no workspace) fails safe toward **not** flagging a stall -- an inconclusive check must never manufacture a false positive. Visual tmux pane text is never part of this evidence set at all, per the rule's own explicit prohibition.

Wired into `write_stuck_tasks_heartbeat()` (new `stalled_running_tasks` parameter, defaulting to an empty list so pre-existing callers/tests are unaffected) and `main()`'s own tick.

## Tests
9 new real tests, `tests/test_rule5_real_stall_detection.py`:
- Real `/proc/<pid>/stat` parsing against this test process's own real PID (not a mock), including a parenthesized-comm-field edge case
- Cold-start / no-process / real-delta-comparison CPU-activity cases
- Real file-mtime checks against a real temp workspace
- An end-to-end case proving the AND-of-all-five requirement: a task with 4 stale signals but one fresh file is correctly **not** flagged
- A fail-safe case for a missing `umr_tasks` row

9/9 pass. All pre-existing suites (46 tests total across Rules 1-4, `test_stuck_task_heartbeat.py`, `test_pm_triage.py`, OCID-artifact-links, DB-path-resolution) re-run clean after resolving a real rebase conflict against Rule 4's own `write_stuck_tasks_heartbeat()` changes (both real additions -- `real_task_counts` and `stalled_running_tasks` -- kept together). `python3 -m py_compile` clean.

## Note on PR #31's own follow-up findings
PR #31's real independent review found 4 real, non-blocking follow-up gaps in Rule 4's own `compute_real_task_counts()` (unaccounted `dispatched`/`sigterm_sent` statuses, an over-broad `retrying` count, dead code, an unused parameter). Not fixed in this PR -- flagged for a separate follow-up, kept out of this PR's scope.

## Scope note
This PR implements Rule 5 only. Rules 6-7 remain separately scoped.

## Summary
Second real installment of the OCID-068 seven-rule guardrails addendum (Rule 2 of 7, following Rule 1/PR #26). Per `UMR-20260804-203846-e722` (checkpoint refresh, confirms Rule 1 genuinely merged via PR #26 commit `29a153b`, directs continued real implementation of Rules 2-7 one at a time). Checked for active/duplicate work first (2 running workers were unrelated older tasks; a genuinely duplicate automated worker on this same scope was already found and stopped earlier this session, per PR #26's own report).

**Rule 2** (verbatim, from `UMR-20260804-180711-7f96`): "every dispatch shall return exactly one of five allowed results, success, failed, blocked, rejected, or cancelled, with no other state permitted, no silent failure, and no empty output, and on failure the dispatch must return a real error id, a real root cause, real evidence, and a real next action, then stop."

## What changed
`dispatch_one()` already has a real, richer internal `action` vocabulary (`idle`, `deferred`, `frozen`, `dispatched`, `rejected_duplicate_pr`, `emergency_stopped`, `superboss_unavailable`) that other real code (`dispatch-tick.py`, `run_tick()`'s own loop-stop condition, existing tests) depends on. Rather than replace it, `classify_dispatch_outcome()` is a new, additive classification layer that maps every real dispatch attempt onto exactly one of Rule 2's five canonical outcomes:

- `idle`/`would_dispatch` -> `outcome=None` (not a real dispatch attempt at all -- queue empty / dry-run preview -- so the 5-value enum deliberately does not apply here, rather than fabricating a value to force a fit)
- `dispatched` with `result.status=="running"` -> `success`
- `dispatched` with `result.status=="failed"` -> `failed`, with `root_cause`/`evidence` pulled from `_perform_spawn()`'s own real `outputs.error`/`outputs.stderr`
- `emergency_stopped`/`frozen`/`superboss_unavailable`/`deferred` -> `blocked` (real, expected transient blocks, not task-specific failures)

## Summary
First real installment of the OCID-068 seven-rule guardrails addendum -- Rule 1 only (of 7). Per `UMR-20260804-194355-be9c` (part of a five-way parallel expedite directive): checked for active/duplicate work first (none found -- fresh clone `git grep`/`git log --all --grep` across `veridian-scripts` for the UMR string returned zero matches, and no running `veridian-worker@*`/`veridian-supervisor@*` unit addresses this scope), then began real implementation.

**Rule 1** (verbatim, from `UMR-20260804-180711-7f96`): "one logical task shall have exactly one OCID, exactly one UMR, and one canonical task identity, and any retry, resume, redispatch, supervisor, worker, executor, or restart shall reuse the existing UMR rather than minting a new one."

## The real, previously-documented gap
`resource_governor.py`'s own module comment (above `find_active_umr_by_identity()`) already states the limitation this PR fixes: that function "only rejects a SECOND submission while the FIRST is still active (queued/dispatched/running); it cannot see a prior run that already finished." Since `submit()` always called `upsert_umr_task()` with no `umr_id`, and `upsert_umr_task()`'s own logic is `record.get("umr_id") or _new_id("UMR")`, every retry/resume of a task whose prior run went terminal minted a brand-new UMR. The real caller this matters for is `dispatch-tick.py`'s `resume_interrupted_workers_tick()`, which reuses `task_identity=task_id` stably across every resume attempt for a given worker task -- exactly the retry/resume/redispatch case Rule 1 names.

## What changed
- `superboss-register.py`: new `find_most_recent_umr_by_identity()` -- the complement of `find_active_umr_by_identity()`, returning any row (active or terminal) for a `task_identity`, most recent first.
- `resource_governor.py`'s `submit()`: when no ACTIVE duplicate exists but a prior (terminal) row for the same `task_identity` does, its `umr_id` is now reused via `upsert_umr_task()`'s existing `ON CONFLICT(umr_id) DO UPDATE` path, instead of minting a fresh one.
- Owner-dispatch callers (`dispatch-owner-task.sh`) mint a fresh `timestamp+pid` `task_identity` per call, so this never fires for them -- only a genuine identity collision (by construction, a retry/resume of the same real task) reuses a `umr_id`.
- Original `ts_submitted` is preserved across reuse (already excluded from the UPDATE SET list, same convention as `tenant_id`/UTM fields).

## Tests
4 new real tests, `tests/test_umr_reuse_on_resume.py`, against a real isolated scratch SQLite DB with the real schema (never the live production DB):
- `test_terminal_prior_run_is_reused_not_reminted`
- `test_active_prior_run_still_rejected_as_duplicate_not_reused` (proves the existing concurrency guard is unweakened)
- `test_fresh_task_identity_gets_a_new_umr_as_before`
- `test_reused_umr_preserves_original_ts_submitted`

All 4/4 pass. `python3 -m py_compile` clean on both touched files.

## Scope note
This PR implements Rule 1 only. Rules 2-7 of the same addendum are real, separately scoped pieces of work (dispatch return-contract enforcement, validation-before-minting ordering, PM-visible real counts, combined-evidence stall detection, broader zero-duplication checks, and a strict completion definition) -- not attempted here, to keep this change small, focused, and reviewable against a live, every-30-second-cycle governance chokepoint.

Cites `UMR-20260804-194355-be9c` and `UMR-20260804-170055-a069`.

## Summary
Owner directive **UMR-20260804-194230** ("Deterministic canonical database path resolution, full
spec"), a follow-on to **UMR-20260804-180142-676d** (which carried only a short summary),
related to **OCID-068** governance runtime consolidation and **UMR-20260804-170055-a069**.

`resolve_superboss_db_path()` in `superboss-register.py` already implements the exact real
5-step algorithm this directive specifies -- it was built and merged via PR #20 (`5130153`)
and independently hardened via PR #21 (`a277ebb`, `5c7d951`):

1. Read `SUPERBOSS_REGISTER_DB` from the environment.
2. If set, exists on disk, and is non-zero size, use it as the candidate.
3. Otherwise use the fixed default `/opt/veridian/ai-os/memory/superboss-register.sqlite`.
4. Before any read/write/register/update, verify in order: file exists; non-zero size;
   real SQLite header magic bytes (`b"SQLite format 3\x00"`); a real `umr_tasks` table via a
   direct `sqlite_master` query.
5. Only once every check passes does `DB_PATH` get set to the candidate.

Any failure raises the real, named `SuperbossDbPathError` stating which check failed, the exact
path checked, the exact size found, and the reason -- execution stops, never a silent fallback.
It permanently keeps failing against the known stale zero-byte decoy at
`/opt/veridian/ai-os/superboss-register.sqlite`. `resource_governor.py` and every other real
caller still read this module's `DB_PATH` through the existing importlib-by-file-path loader --
**no second implementation of this logic exists anywhere in the codebase.**

body:
## Summary — final design (revised after real evidence, see below)

Per Owner directive UMR-20260801-190119-ff34, reversing this same branch's earlier approach (UMR-20260801-172407-ae58). **Real evidence drove the pivot**: swap hit 100% exhaustion with only 3 of the then-current 5-slot cap actually running. That's the key finding — the box can run out of real headroom *without the slot count ever reaching the ceiling*, fixed or dynamic, because per-worker memory/swap use ramps up *during* a worker's own run (a build/compile spike), not just at spawn time. A smarter ceiling number doesn't fix that, and a dynamic ceiling computing above 5 on a seemingly-idle box would have made the failure mode worse, not better.

**Final design:**
- `CONCURRENCY_CAP` is a genuinely fixed constant again — **5**, the Owner's own already-vetted number. `VERIDIAN_DISPATCH_CONCURRENCY_CAP` env override works identically to before.
- `has_resource_headroom()` is a new, independent, real-time veto — real `/proc/meminfo` + load average, re-read fresh on every `has_free_slot()` call — that can refuse a new dispatch even when the slot count is still under 5, if real headroom is already tight. **Both the fixed cap and the veto must pass.**
- Same hard-ceiling (99%, Owner's number, never cross) / backoff (80%, real margin below the hard ceiling) / per-worker-budget (2GB, matches `MemoryHigh=2G`) thresholds carried over from the reverted dynamic-cap attempt — the safety reasoning was sound, only its job changed: sizing a variable ceiling (removed) vs. vetoing an individual dispatch below a fixed ceiling (kept).

## Verified live, not just asserted
`has_resource_headroom()` returned **False against this box's real current state at revision time** — swap was genuinely at ~99.99% used right now, completely independent of any test setup. Direct, unplanned, real-world confirmation of exactly the scenario this change exists to catch.

Also tested synthetically:
- Hard ceiling trips at 99% memory and 99% swap.
- Backoff trips at 85% memory (below the hard ceiling, above the 80% backoff threshold) — confirms it reacts *before* 99%, not at the last moment.
- Healthy case (50% memory, low load) → true.
- Load-based veto trips at load 7.0 vs. an 8-core × 0.8 = 6.4 threshold.
- **The exact combined scenario the Owner described**: 3 of 5 slots used (well under cap), swap deliberately made scarce → `has_free_slot()` correctly refuses. Same 3/5 slots with healthy resources → correctly allows. 5/5 slots with healthy resources → correctly refuses on the fixed cap alone, independent of resource state.

## Preserved, unchanged, re-verified
- `MemoryHigh=2G`/`MemoryMax=3G`/`MemorySwapMax=1G` per-unit cgroup limits.
- No `[Install]` section / no systemd boot-activation path.

## Also fixed
A stale reference this branch's own earlier doc-fix commit introduced: `veridian-worker@.service`'s RCA comment named `compute_dynamic_concurrency_cap()` by name — that function no longer exists after this revert, updated to describe the real final design.

## Documentation check (re-run for the revised design)
`MASTER_INDEX.yaml`, `PROTOCOL_OWNER_AI.yaml`, both READMEs, `dispatch-owner-task.sh`: still zero "CONCURRENCY_CAP"/"cap of 5" hits, no updates needed. `resource_governor.py`'s own comment mentioning `CONCURRENCY_CAP` generically is now *more* accurate than during the dynamic-cap attempt, since the constant is genuinely fixed again — left unchanged.

## Honest history
This PR's own commits show the real evolution: dynamic ceiling attempted first (2 commits), then reverted to fixed-cap + independent real-time veto after live evidence showed the dynamic approach's premise (a smarter ceiling number alone) doesn't address the real failure mode (mid-run resource spikes independent of slot count).
title: fix: CONCURRENCY_CAP=5 fixed + real-time resource-headroom veto (was: dynamic cap)

body:
## Root cause (2026-08-01, 24-unit OOM-kill incident)

The server has a real, working concurrency-governance system --
`dispatch_core.py` (shared flock + `CONCURRENCY_CAP`, default 5) and
`resource_governor.py` (99%-per-metric hard caps, `umr_tasks` queue table)
-- and every real spawn call site in the consolidated tick scripts correctly
routes through `dispatch_core.acquire_dispatch_lock()`/`has_free_slot()`
before starting anything.

**But this governance had zero control over systemd's own native boot-time
activation.** `veridian-task.py`'s `cmd_create` also called `systemctl
--user enable` on every new `veridian-worker@<task-id>.service`, so the
task would survive a reboot mid-work. `enable` wires a unit into
`default.target.wants/`, and **every unit there is started by systemd
itself, in parallel, unconditionally, the instant the box boots** -- with
zero awareness of `dispatch_core`'s lock/cap. On 2026-08-01, 24 accumulated
enabled worker units did exactly that against an 11GB memory cap and
OOM-killed the box. The units themselves are legitimate real in-progress
work (CRM features, PM modules, PR rebases, audits), only disabled today as
an emergency measure -- not deleted.

## Fix

1. **`veridian-task.py` (`cmd_create`)**: removed the `systemctl --user
   enable` call entirely. A worker unit is now only ever started explicitly
   (`systemctl --user start`), never boot-enabled.
2. **`veridian-worker@.service`** (tracked here under `systemd/`, and
   applied live under `~/.config/systemd/user/` on the box): removed the
   `[Install]`/`WantedBy=default.target` section entirely, so `enable`
   is now a hard no-op even if a future call site tries it again --
   confirmed live: `systemctl --user is-enabled` now reports the template
   as `static` ("has no installation config").
3. **`dispatch-tick.py`**: new `resume_interrupted_workers_tick()`, run
   every tick alongside the existing supervisor-sweep / gap-queue /
   module-queue ticks. Finds any `task.yaml` left `pending`/`in_progress`
   whose `veridian-worker@` unit is **not currently active** (the real
   signature of "was mid-work when the box rebooted/crashed, and nothing
   auto-started it") and re-submits it through `resource_governor.py`'s
   `submit()` -- the `umr_tasks` queue, **never a direct systemctl call**
   -- so `dispatch_one()` drains it under the exact same cap/lock and
   4-metric resource gate as any other new task. N interrupted tasks after a
   reboot now trickle back in at the existing cap instead of all firing at
   once.
4. **`test_worker_boot_activation_and_resume.py`**: real, executable test.
   Part 1 spins up a scratch systemd --user unit with no `[Install]`
   section (the fixed shape) and asserts `is-enabled` reports `static`,
   `enable` creates no new `*.wants/` symlink anywhere, and `start`
   still works and runs to completion -- then cleans up completely. Part 2
   exercises `resume_interrupted_workers_tick()` in-process with
   `resource_governor.submit` faked out, asserting: an inactive
   in-progress task gets queued with `action=start`; a task behind a
   *failed* unit gets queued with `action=reset_failed_and_start`; an
   already-active task is skipped, not re-submitted; terminal-status tasks
   (completed/blocked) are never considered; and every submission uses
   `task_kind=systemctl_action` (never `veridian_task_create` -- this is a
   resume, not a new task). All 11 assertions pass.

## Verified live on VERIDIAN-DEV before this commit

- `systemctl --user enable` against the fixed template: no-op, no new
  `default.target.wants/` symlink, unit reports `static`.
- `systemctl --user start` on the same unit: still works, reaches
  `active (running)`.
- Ran the real, updated `dispatch-tick.py` against the live box: it
  correctly found the real 24-unit backlog from
  `DISABLED_WORKER_UNITS_BACKUP_2026-08-01/list.txt` (plus some
  additional, older interrupted tasks the same general check correctly also
  caught) and queued all of them into the real `umr_tasks` table via
  `resource_governor.submit()` -- confirmed via `resource_governor.py
  --query-umr`.
- Actual dispatch of that queue is currently blocked by a **pre-existing**
  `resource_governor` `EMERGENCY_STOP` sentinel from 2026-07-30 (a known,
  already-documented near-zero-metrics false-positive per
  `~/.config/systemd/user/README.md`'s own re-audit notes; current real
  metrics read healthy -- `ram 26%`, everything else `0%`, nothing over
  threshold). I deliberately left this untouched: clearing it requires the
  same explicit operator judgment call as resuming
  `veridian-governor-tick.service` (the service that normally owns/clears
  this exact sentinel), which this task's own scope says must stay paused
  pending explicit Owner instruction. Once cleared, this queue will drain
  automatically at the existing cap.
- Confirmed nothing else already paused was touched: all 20
  `veridian-cron-*`/`veridian-dispatch-tick` timers remain absent/disabled
  (`systemctl --user list-timers` shows only the unrelated system
  `launchpadlib-cache-clean.timer`), `veridian-directive-engine.service`
  and `veridian-governor-tick.service` remain `inactive`/`disabled`, and
  `~/.config/systemd/user/default.target.wants/` still does not exist.

## Note on branch history

This branch was cut from `main-clean`'s current HEAD (the box's actual live
checkout), which already had 3 commits not yet pushed to `origin/main`
before this PR (`1cef3fe`, `75a0999`, `52c8367`) -- pre-existing,
unrelated local work from other sessions, already running live on the box.
This PR's own change is the single commit `fbf0673` on top; the other 3 are
out of scope for this review.

body:
## Summary
Owner report: live PROJEXA site page loading is very slow. Measured the real live app (https://projexa-ai.com) in real Chromium at 1440x900 (real seeded E2E CEO login), found and fixed the real dominant cost.

## Real measurements (`/dashboard`, 4 runs, live site)
- TTFB: 2848-3885ms (mean ~3.3s), `cache-control: no-store` + `x-vercel-cache: MISS` on every run — never cached, paid every visit, not a cold-start artifact.
- FCP/LCP fire ~150-300ms after the document arrives; TBT is 0ms — the document response, not client JS/hydration, is what's slow.
- Total JS 1.08MB / 16 chunks. Total CSS 143.1KB / 2 files (matches the ~134KB cited in the spec).

## Two spec-flagged theories, tested and eliminated by real build measurement
- **`transpilePackages` for `@fchecklist/veridian-ui-kit`**: removing it breaks the build entirely (ui-kit ships raw `.tsx`) — load-bearing, not optional. Real footprint: 36KB of 58MB server output, a few seconds of a ~27s clean build. Not dominant.
- **Tailwind `@source` directive** (added in 3f0c411): rebuilt with/without it. Real delta: **+2,682 bytes** (+35 utility rules) on the ~131KB main CSS bundle — not "the whole ui-kit utility surface," not material. Left untouched (load-bearing for the layout fix; not inflated enough to narrow).

## Root cause
`dashboard/page.tsx` awaited 4+ independent network round trips sequentially on a never-cached route: org/membership lookup → VERIDIAN `/dashboard` fetch → VERIDIAN `/currencies` fetch (independent, but sequential for no reason) → a fully redundant live `supabase.auth.getUser()` call for a value `requireAuth()` already resolves from the JWT it already verified. That redundant-`getUser()` anti-pattern was already fixed everywhere else in the app except this one page (grep-confirmed).

## Fix
Single `requireAuth()` call (removes the redundant round trip) + `Promise.allSettled` around the two independent VERIDIAN calls. Scope kept to this one file — checked `dashboard/overview/page.tsx` and the rest of `src/app`; no other page has this pattern.

## Verification
Clean `tsc --noEmit`, clean `eslint`, full `next build` all pass. Deployed a real Vercel preview of the fix to get live after-numbers, but Vercel SSO deployment protection blocked reaching it, and disabling that project-wide setting to work around it needs Owner sign-off (outward-facing security change) — not done unilaterally. See `progress/task-20260817-042949-measure-and-fix-slow-page-loading-on-the.md` for full before-numbers and reasoning, plus a follow-up item to re-measure post-merge.

Column proportions (10/50/40) untouched. No ui-kit changes — no tag/pin/lockfile change needed.

Real, working Playwright E2E tests for the 11 Batch B modules (**materials, inventory, procurement, purchase-orders, vendors, labour, ffe, floor-plans, mood-boards, permits, documents**) + a non-admin (site-supervisor) access check — **12 spec files, 31 tests** — run against the live `https://projexa-ai.com` deployment and the real seeded "Meridian Construction Group (E2E Test Org)" test org.
